method: Each of the 416 Comparator statements at the pinned commit was classified by reading OpenAI's scope note for its family (lean/docs/<family>.md), the challenge file and its configuration (lean/ComparatorChallenges/<Id>.lean and .json), and the theorem-like statements in the introduction of each accompanying manuscript (data/manuscripts.json, statements with headline true), with the manuscript's TeX source consulted where these were not enough. The reading was done by an AI agent (Claude Code); no named person has yet reviewed the rows. Every row quotes the scope note verbatim in scope_quote. paper_headline names the manuscript statement the class is judged against: the paper statement the challenge states, for headline and headline-part rows; the headline theorem that the challenge's statement follows from or weakens, for consequence and weaker rows, and the headline result supported for supporting rows. A paper's headline theorem is its main result as the paper states it; a statement the paper derives as a corollary counts as a consequence even when it appears in the introduction. Where a scope note and a challenge file differ, the class follows the challenge file and the explanation says so. Comparator definition holes and placeholder axioms are mentioned in the explanation. The classes describe coverage, meaning which paper result a statement is aimed at and how much of it the statement asserts; they are not a verdict that the Lean statement means what the paper means.

classes.headline: states a headline theorem of an accompanying paper as stated, allowing harmless formalisation choices
classes.headline-part: states one part or case of a multi-part headline theorem; the other parts are outside this statement
classes.consequence: states a corollary or application of the headline theorem rather than the theorem itself
classes.weaker: states a weaker form of the headline: fewer cases, worse constants, extra hypotheses, or an eventual or qualitative version of a quantitative claim
classes.supporting: states an auxiliary or supporting result, not a headline result
classes.unclear: the materials do not settle the class; the explanation says what would

rows.scope_quote: The formalization gives $\theta=7/8$ for the Riemann zeta function and every Dirichlet $L$-function, uniformly over all positive moduli and all characters.
rows.explanation: States the Dirichlet L-function case of the main theorem, for every modulus and character, with the pole of a principal character at s = 1 excluded. The Hecke case over Q(√−3) is a separate statement.

rows.scope_quote: It also establishes the same bound for finite-order Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$.
rows.explanation: States the first assertion of the main theorem, the 7/8 half-plane for finite-order Hecke L-functions over Q(√−3), using definitions of these L-functions made in the challenge file. The Dirichlet and zeta cases of the theorem are separate statements.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization gives $\theta=7/8$ for the Riemann zeta function and every Dirichlet $L$-function, uniformly over all positive moduli and all characters.
rows.explanation: States the case of the Riemann zeta function in the main theorem: no zero with real part above 7/8. The Dirichlet and Hecke cases of the same theorem are separate statements (DirichletSevenEighths, HeckeSevenEighths).

rows.scope_quote: There is one constant $c>0$ such that every primitive nonprincipal real Dirichlet character of conductor $q\ge3$ and every real zero $0<\beta<1$ of its $L$-function satisfy $1-\beta\ge c/\log q$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the Landau–Siegel paper: an absolute constant c > 0 with (1 − β) log q ≥ c for every real zero β in (0, 1) of every primitive nonprincipal real Dirichlet L-function of conductor q ≥ 3.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves that Catalan's constant $G=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}(-1)^j/(2j+1)^2$ is irrational. This is the mathematical assertion in the paper's title.
rows.explanation: States the paper's main theorem, the irrationality of Catalan's constant.

rows.scope_quote: For two one-bounded multiplicative functions, if at least one is uniformly nonpretentious against all Dirichlet-character twists with frequency $|t|\le N$, then their shifted and nonproportional affine correlation sums divided by $N$ tend to zero.
rows.explanation: States the binary corrected Elliott theorem for ordinary averages under uniform nonpretentiousness of one factor, one of the paper's two main theorems.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves ordinary two-point cancellation for multiplicative functions. For the Liouville function on every fixed pair of nonproportional affine forms, the correlation sum up to $X$ is $O(X/(\log X)^c)$ for an absolute $c>0$, with the implied constant depending on the forms.
rows.explanation: States the logarithmic saving for Liouville correlations on nonproportional affine forms, together with the binary corrected Elliott theorem and its affine corollary: the three theorem-like statements of the paper's introduction.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization establishes this for the rational solution space of antisymmetry, the three-term equation, and the four-strand pentagon with the Ihara bracket. It also gives the corresponding continuous isomorphism after completion by weight.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: the rational Grothendieck–Teichmüller Lie algebra, defined by antisymmetry, the three-term relation and the pentagon, is freely generated by one element in each odd weight, with the completed isomorphism. The note lists the regularised-transport proposition and graph-complex consequences as not included.

rows.scope_quote: The selected statement proves this uniqueness; existence of a field isomorphism for every admissible Galois-data isomorphism is outside it.
rows.explanation: States the uniqueness half of the reconstruction theorem: field isomorphisms inducing the same Galois-data isomorphism agree modulo Frobenius. Existence of a field isomorphism for every admissible Galois-data isomorphism is outside the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves the joint Dickman law in ordinary natural density: for every $0<a,b<1$, the density of integers satisfying $P^+(n)\le n^a$ and $P^+(n+1)\le n^b$ tends to $\rho(1/a)\rho(1/b)$, where $\rho$ is the Dickman function.
rows.explanation: States the joint Dickman law in natural density, as in the main theorem, and the corollary that each strict ordering of P⁺(n) and P⁺(n+1) has density 1/2.

rows.scope_quote: The linked statements include the full result and its two-infinite-summands case.
rows.explanation: States Ostmann's inverse Goldbach conjecture as in the paper's main theorem, together with the case of two infinite summands.

rows.scope_quote: For any two sets $A,B$ of nonnegative integers, each containing at least two elements, the symmetric difference between their sumset $A+B$ and the set of primes is infinite.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem directly: for sets A, B of natural numbers with at least two elements each, (A + B) and the primes have infinite symmetric difference.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves equidistribution of volume-weighted torus packets for totally real number fields of every fixed prime degree at least five. For any sequence of full lattices whose multiplier-order discriminants tend to infinity, the packet measures converge weakly to Haar probability measure and form a tight family, so no mass escapes. Arbitrary local homothety types are allowed, and the fields may vary along the sequence.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: weak convergence of prime-degree torus-packet measures to Haar probability measure, with tightness, for arbitrary local type.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves that the irrationality exponent of $\pi$ is exactly two. For every $\nu>2$, all sufficiently large positive denominators $q$ satisfy $|\pi-p/q|\ge q^{-\nu}$ for every integer numerator $p$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem that the irrationality exponent of π is 2. The paper's corollary on convergence of the Flint–Hills series is outside the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result proves positive-density power-free values for every integer polynomial $f$ irreducible over $\mathbb Q$ of degree $d\ge4$. Put $k=d-2$ and assume no prime $k$th power divides every value of $f$. Then the number of positive integers $n\le X$ for which $f(n)$ is $k$-free is $c_fX+o_f(X)$, where $c_f>0$ is the convergent product of local factors.
rows.explanation: States the all-degree form of the power-free density theorem (degree d ≥ 4, k = d − 2), which contains the main theorem for degrees 4 to 8 as a case; the paper obtains degrees above 8 from Browning's theorem.

rows.scope_quote: The earlier quadratic bound is also retained as a separate statement; the optimal order of growth is not determined.
rows.explanation: States the earlier quadratic bound h(k) ≤ Ck², which the main theorem improves by the factor (log log 3k)²; the note keeps it as a separate statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves the paper's strengthened Jacobsthal bound $h(k)\le Ck^2/(\log\log(3k))^2$ for one absolute $C>0$ and every $k\ge1$. Intervals may begin at any signed integer.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem h(k) ≤ Ck²/(log log 3k)² for every k ≥ 1, with intervals allowed to start at any integer.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves the sharp-cutoff asymptotic with main term $\frac65c_*X^{5/6}/\log X$, where $c_*=(2\pi)^{2/3}/(3\Gamma(2/3))$. It also proves the corresponding angular comparison for every integer Fourier mode and cancellation of order $o(X^{5/6}/\log X)$ for each fixed nonzero mode. All primary Eisenstein primes are included, without an extra conjectural premise.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem, the sharp first-moment asymptotic for cubic Gauss sums over all primary Eisenstein primes, together with the angular comparison and cancellation in each fixed mode.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization constructs the paper's explicit positive main term from finite arithmetic approximants and proves that their ratio tends to one. In particular, $V(cx)/V(x)\to c$ for every fixed $c>0$, answering the Erdős–Hall regular-variation question.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem (the explicit asymptotic for the number of totients up to x and V(cx)/V(x) → c), together with the asymptotic of the companion theorem for totients whose least preimage lies between kx and (k+1)x.

rows.scope_quote: The associated coefficient is positive under the stated existence condition; when no totient $d$ satisfies $kd<\ell(d)$, the count and coefficient are identically zero.
rows.explanation: States case (ii) of the companion theorem: when no totient d has least preimage above kd, the count and its coefficient vanish identically. The asymptotic and the positive case are in TotientAsymptotic.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves that every $a/b$ with $1\le a<b$ has such an expansion and that the largest minimum length at denominator $b$ is $\Theta(\log\log b)$. If $F(k)$ counts exact $k$-term expansions of $1$, it also proves $\log\log F(k)=\Theta(k)$ and bounds every denominator in such an expansion.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem (the largest minimum expansion length at denominator b is of order log log b) together with the counting corollary and the results on prescribed denominators.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves that every $a/b$ with $1\le a<b$ has such an expansion and that the largest minimum length at denominator $b$ is $\Theta(\log\log b)$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: the largest minimum length of an Egyptian-fraction expansion at denominator b is of order log log b.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized supplement proves that the indices $n$ for which $p_n/n<p_{n+1}/(n+1)$ have positive lower asymptotic density, where $p_n$ is the $n$th prime. Thus the normalized prime sequence has a positive-density set of increases. This is the prime-ratio corollary associated with the paper's theorem on a positive lower density of large prime gaps.
rows.explanation: The statement's first conjunct is the main theorem (for every C > 0, a positive proportion of n ≤ N have p_{n+1} − p_n > C log p_n) and its second is the prime-ratio corollary. The scope note describes only the corollary.

rows.scope_quote: The linked formalization proves a supporting compatibility result for its marked-surface construction.
rows.explanation: States a compatibility property of the paper's marked-surface construction, one of the five supporting comparisons named in the Comparator README. Potential integral density itself is outside the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result gives a negative answer for every real step bound $D$. More strongly, one finite bound depending only on $D$ limits the size of every connected component of the bounded-step graph and the length of every injective bounded-step walk.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: for every step bound D, the connected components of the bounded-step Gaussian-prime graph have uniformly bounded size, so no infinite bounded-step walk exists.

rows.scope_quote: The finite-dimension and negative-base branches of the paper's additivity theorem are outside this selected statement.
rows.explanation: States the negative-fibre branch of the logarithmic additivity theorem: if the fibre over a very general point has logarithmic Kodaira dimension −∞, so does the total space. The finite-dimension and negative-base branches are outside the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result establishes this for every smooth integral complex projective surface $S$ and ample line bundle $L$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the Seshadri paper: for every smooth projective surface and ample line bundle, the multipoint Seshadri constant at very general points is maximal once r exceeds a threshold depending on the pair.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization establishes this inequality simultaneously for all curves and multiplicity vectors outside one countable union of proper Zariski-closed exceptional sets with nonempty complement.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: Nagata's inequality for all curves and multiplicity vectors at r ≥ 10 points outside one countable union of proper closed subsets.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result gives an explicit finite-type complex domain $A$ of Krull dimension four with $A[w]\cong\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_5]$ but $A\not\cong\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_4]$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: an explicit complex domain A of dimension four with A[w] isomorphic to a polynomial ring in five variables and A not isomorphic to one in four. The stable-coordinate corollary is not included.

rows.scope_quote: For every $n\ge4$, the formalized counterexample gives $F\in\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ with quotient $\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(F)\cong\mathbb C[y_1,\ldots,y_{n-1}]$, although $F$ is not a coordinate.
rows.explanation: States the paper's corollary for every n ≥ 4 in existential form: some polynomial in n variables has quotient isomorphic to a polynomial ring in n − 1 variables without being a coordinate. The main theorem's explicit four-variable polynomial is not named in the statement.

rows.scope_quote: A companion gives $n-1$ commuting, locally nilpotent derivations, linearly independent over the polynomial ring, whose common kernel is generated by the construction's explicit polynomial and contains no ambient coordinate. The extra $n-4$ derivations are ordinary partial derivatives in the added variables.
rows.explanation: States a companion application of the paper's explicit polynomial: n − 1 commuting, locally nilpotent, linearly independent derivations whose common kernel is generated by it and contains no coordinate. This is not one of the paper's displayed theorem statements.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization gives an explicit degree-five polynomial in four complex variables that becomes a coordinate after adjoining one variable but is not a coordinate in four variables. Every fiber is isomorphic to affine three-space, yet no fiber can be carried to a coordinate hyperplane by an ambient polynomial automorphism.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the four-variable paper (the explicit degree-five polynomial is a coordinate after adjoining one variable but not before) together with its corollary on nonrectifiable fibres.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized counterexample starts with a rank-two algebraic bundle $G$ on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$. Its coordinatewise power pullbacks, tensored with $\mathcal O(1,1)$, are ample for every positive power but admit no such metric for all sufficiently large powers.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: an explicit rank-two bundle on the quadric surface whose twisted power pullbacks are ample for every power but carry no Griffiths-positive metric for all large powers. The separate very-ampleness result is not included.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result gives an affirmative answer for a compact connected Kähler manifold whose tangent bundle splits into two positive-rank, integrable holomorphic subbundles. The universal cover is a product of connected simply connected complex manifolds of the prescribed dimensions, and the differential identifies the two tangent factors with the original summands.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: for a compact Kähler manifold whose tangent bundle splits into two integrable holomorphic subbundles, the universal cover is a product matching the splitting. The paper's corollaries are not included.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves integrability of both summands in a holomorphic splitting of the tangent bundle of a rationally connected projective manifold. More precisely, for a compact connected complex manifold of dimension at least two with a projective embedding witnessing rational connectedness, each positive-rank summand of a holomorphic tangent-bundle splitting is integrable.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the integrability paper: on a rationally connected projective manifold, both summands of a holomorphic tangent splitting are integrable. The product-decomposition corollary is outside the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result answers the paper's symmetry question affirmatively. A nonempty connected bounded semialgebraic subset, relatively open in a complex affine algebraic set, is smooth and biholomorphic to a bounded symmetric domain whenever a discrete group acts properly and holomorphically with compact quotient.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: a connected bounded semialgebraic domain with a properly discontinuous cocompact group of biholomorphisms is biholomorphic to a bounded symmetric domain.

rows.scope_quote: Uniform Cartier sections, bounded klt complements, and the paper's real-boundary and companion conclusions are outside this supporting statement.
rows.explanation: States a local compactness lemma about chart-field retractions used towards uniform Cartier sections, one of the five supporting comparisons named in the Comparator README. Uniform Cartier sections and bounded complements are outside it.

rows.scope_quote: The same Comparator file also states Koebe's circle-domain theorem, which gives a circle-domain representative for every domain in the Riemann sphere.
rows.explanation: The file states the main theorems of both accompanying papers: Koebe's circle-domain theorem for every domain in the Riemann sphere, and conformal rigidity of circle domains with conformally removable boundary.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization establishes this interval, along with area integrability of $|f'|^t$ for univalent disk maps when $-2<t<2/3$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: Brennan's conjecture for 4/3 < s < 4, the equivalent range −2 < t < 2/3 for univalent disk maps, the inverse-square integral-means bound and the value B_S(−2) = 1.

rows.scope_quote: The Koebe map and its inverse give divergence at all four boundary exponents.
rows.explanation: States the paper's sharpness corollary: the Koebe function and its inverse make the integrals diverge at the four endpoint exponents. This complements the main theorem rather than following from it.

rows.scope_quote: The underlying estimate gives constants $0<\varepsilon<1/4$ and $C<\infty$ such that the normalized circular mean of $|f'|^{-1}$ is at most $C(1-r)^{-1/4+\varepsilon}$ for every normalized univalent disk map and $1/2\le r<1$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the strict-bound paper: constants 0 < ε < 1/4 and C with the circular mean of |f′|^{-1} at most C(1 − r)^{-1/4+ε}, with the consequence B_b(−1) < 1/4 against Kraetzer's prediction.

rows.scope_quote: For every integer $d\ge2$ and compact set $E\subset\mathbb R^d$ with Hausdorff dimension greater than $d/2$, the set $\{\lVert x-y\rVert:x,y\in E\}$ has positive Lebesgue measure.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: in every dimension d ≥ 2, a compact set of Hausdorff dimension above d/2 has a distance set of positive Lebesgue measure.

rows.scope_quote: The linked statements include both this all-dimensional result and the earlier planar case.
rows.explanation: States the planar case d = 2 of the main theorem, the earlier result that the note keeps beside the all-dimensional statement.

rows.scope_quote:
The formalization proves this for every measurable complex-valued function on $\mathbb T=\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$ satisfying $\int_{\mathbb T}|f|\log(2+|f|)<\infty$. Outside one measurable null set,
$\sum_{k=-N}^{N}\widehat f(k)e^{ikx}\to f(x)$ along the full sequence $N\to\infty$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: symmetric Fourier partial sums of every function in L log L of the circle converge almost everywhere.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization gives real Littlewood polynomials of every sufficiently large length whose maximum modulus on the unit circle is at most $(1+\eta)\sqrt N$ for any fixed $\eta>0$. Thus the smallest possible maximum is asymptotically minimal through all integer lengths.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: for every η > 0 and every large length N there is a real Littlewood polynomial with maximum modulus at most (1 + η)√N on the unit circle.

rows.scope_quote: A further statement chooses one family of real sign polynomials for all lengths such that, for every fixed finite $p>0$, the $L^p$ mean of $\bigl||P_N(z)|/\sqrt N-1\bigr|$ on the unit circle tends to zero. The results are existential and do not give an effective convergence rate or a signing algorithm.
rows.explanation: States the paper's finite-exponent flatness corollary (Section 7): one sign family of every length with ||P_N|/√N − 1| tending to 0 in every L^p, p < ∞. The two-sided ultraflat bound of the family's later paper is not part of the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result proves that bounded Riesz transforms force quantitative uniform rectifiability in higher codimension. For $d\ge4$ and $2\le n\le d-2$, an $n$-Ahlfors–David regular measure whose positive hard truncations have one uniform $L^2$ operator bound has big pieces of Lipschitz images.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem in quantitative form: an n-Ahlfors–David regular measure in codimension at least two with bounded Riesz transforms has big pieces of Lipschitz images, with constants depending only on the stated data. The variation and principal-value corollary is not included.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result proves the symmetric maximal estimate for the triangular Hilbert transform: for arbitrary complex $F,G\in L^3(\mathbb R^2)$, the $L^{3/2}$ norm of the supremum over all finite hard-truncation intervals is at most $C\|F\|_3\|G\|_3$ for one absolute constant $C$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: the L^3 × L^3 → L^{3/2} bound for the maximal triangular Hilbert transform at the symmetric point, with one absolute constant.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves uniform $L^2$ bounds for short Hilbert transforms along Lipschitz unit vector fields in the plane, including fields depending on both coordinates. For Lipschitz constant $K>0$, every hard truncation with $0<\varepsilon\le R\le1/(10^6K)$ has one universal $L^2$ bound on Schwartz functions, independent of the inner cutoff.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: uniform L² bounds for short hard truncations of Hilbert transforms along Lipschitz unit vector fields, with the principal-value and weak-(2,2) consequences stated in the theorem.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves the dyadic case of the Erdős similarity conjecture. For every $0<\eta<1$, it constructs a compact set $E\subset[0,1]$ of measure greater than $1-\eta$ that contains no affine copy of $\{2^{-n}:n\ge1\}$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: for every η in (0, 1) a compact subset of [0, 1] of measure above 1 − η containing no affine copy of {2^{-n}}. The geometric case of the family's later paper is not part of the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves that every real $f\in W^{1,1}(\mathbb R^2)$ has a maximal function that is finite almost everywhere, belongs to $W^{1,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, and has a globally integrable weak gradient satisfying $\|\nabla Mf\|_1\le C\|\nabla f\|_1$ for one absolute constant $C$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: for real f in W^{1,1}(R²) the centred disk maximal function is locally W^{1,1} with ‖∇Mf‖₁ ≤ C‖∇f‖₁. A BV extension is outside the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The earlier signed finite-band estimate for smooth compactly supported functions is also retained. The general endpoint statement covers the Sobolev setting of the paper; a BV extension is outside these statements.
rows.explanation: States the paper's signed finite-band proposition for smooth compactly supported functions, an earlier estimate the note keeps beside the endpoint statement; it is a step towards the main theorem rather than the theorem itself.

rows.scope_quote:
For every $n\ge1$ and compact convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$ with nonempty interior, the formalization proves
$\inf_{z\in\mathrm{int}\,K}|K|\,|(K-z)^\circ|\ge (n+1)^{n+1}/(n!)^2$.
Equality holds exactly when $K$ is a simplex.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the general Mahler paper: the volume product, minimised over interior centres, is at least (n + 1)^{n+1}/(n!)², with equality exactly for simplices. The functional inequality is outside the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization establishes this for every $n\ge1$ and characterizes equality exactly by invertible linear images of Hanner bodies, built from intervals using Cartesian products and convex-hull joins.
rows.explanation: States the inequality |K||K°| ≥ 4^n/n! of the main theorem for every origin-symmetric convex body. The equality characterisation by Hanner bodies, the other half of the theorem, is the separate statement SymmetricMahlerEquality.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization establishes this for every $n\ge1$ and characterizes equality exactly by invertible linear images of Hanner bodies, built from intervals using Cartesian products and convex-hull joins.
rows.explanation: States the equality case of the main theorem: the volume product equals 4^n/n! exactly for linear images of Hanner bodies. The inequality itself is the separate statement MahlerConjecture.

rows.scope_quote: For an origin-symmetric convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, the formalized result determines the symplectic ball capacity of $\mathrm{int}\,K\times\mathrm{int}\,K^\circ$: its Gromov width is $4$, and every ball of capacity $0<c<4$ embeds symplectically into it. The normalization assigns capacity $\pi r^2$ to a ball of radius $r$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the symplectic paper: for origin-symmetric K in dimension n ≥ 2, int K × int K° has Gromov width 4, every ball of capacity below 4 embedding symplectically.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization establishes this for every convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$ and every $n\ge4$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: Petty's projection inequality for every convex body in dimension n ≥ 4, with equality exactly for ellipsoids.

rows.scope_quote: Thus the proposed maximum fails in dimension $20$. The paper's exponential-factor result for every sufficiently large dimension is not included.
rows.explanation: States the negation of the simplex upper bound in dimension 20 (some convex body has larger normalised projection volume than the simplex), which follows from the main theorem's explicit computation. The explicit body and ratio are the separate statement ProjectionVolume.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized counterexample is the product of two ten-dimensional simplices.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: the product of two ten-dimensional simplices has normalised projection volume exceeding that of the twenty-dimensional simplex by the stated ratio. The exponential-factor result for large dimensions is not included.

rows.scope_quote: For every bag-size bound $k\ge2$, there is a constant $C(k)$ such that the weighted shortest-path metric of every nonempty finite connected graph with a tree decomposition of bag size at most $k$ embeds into finite-dimensional real $L_1$ with distortion at most $C(k)$. Edge lengths may be arbitrary positive real numbers, and the constant is independent of the graph and decomposition size.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the treewidth paper: for each bag-size bound k ≥ 2, a constant C(k) bounds the L1 distortion of every weighted graph with a tree decomposition of bag size at most k.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result gives one constant $C$ for every finite connected planar graph with arbitrary positive real edge lengths: its weighted shortest-path metric embeds into real $L_1$ with distortion at most $C$. The constant is independent of the number of vertices and the ratios between edge lengths; singleton graphs are included.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: one constant bounds the L1 distortion of the shortest-path metric of every finite connected planar graph with positive edge lengths.

rows.scope_quote: It also constructs sharp radial Schwartz minorants for every Gaussian potential: each minorant lies below the Gaussian, has nonnegative real Fourier transform, agrees with the Gaussian at nonzero triangular-lattice points, and vanishes on nonzero dual-lattice points after Fourier transformation. For the stated parameter range, the formalization includes the explicit atomic interpolation construction.
rows.explanation: States the paper's sharp Gaussian minorant theorem for every α > 0, including the atomic interpolation construction for α ≥ 1.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization constructs a radial Schwartz function $f$ on $\mathbb R^2$ with $\widehat f(0)=1$, $f(0)=2/\sqrt3$, $\widehat f$ real and nonnegative everywhere, and $f(x)\le0$ whenever $\|x\|\ge1$. These are the sharp Fourier certificate conditions yielding density $\pi/(2\sqrt3)$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the packing paper: a radial Schwartz function meeting the sharp Cohn–Elkies conditions for density π/(2√3). The uniqueness statement for periodic equality cases is outside it.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves that the density-one triangular lattice minimizes lower energy per particle among all locally finite planar configurations of centered-disk density one, for every nonnegative completely monotone function of squared distance. Infinite energies are allowed in the comparison.
rows.explanation: States the paper's universal energy theorem: the density-one triangular lattice minimises lower energy per particle for every nonnegative completely monotone potential among configurations of centred-disk density one.

rows.scope_quote: It also constructs sharp radial Schwartz minorants for every Gaussian potential: each minorant lies below the Gaussian, has nonnegative real Fourier transform, agrees with the Gaussian at nonzero triangular-lattice points, and vanishes on nonzero dual-lattice points after Fourier transformation. For the stated parameter range, the formalization includes the explicit atomic interpolation construction.
rows.explanation: States the paper's sharp Gaussian minorant theorem for every α > 0 with the construction for α ≥ 1; it differs from AtomicGaussian only in how the construction is packaged.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result proves, for every dimension $n\ge1$, such bodies $K,L\subset\mathbb R^n$, and $0\le t\le1$, that their logarithmic Wulff combination has volume at least $|K|^{1-t}|L|^t$. It assumes neither boundary smoothness nor coordinatewise unconditionality.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: the logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski inequality for origin-symmetric convex bodies in every dimension. The L_p corollary is not part of the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization determines the order of the largest covering density in dimension $n$. For all sufficiently large $n$, the suprema of translative covering density and lattice covering density are each bounded above and below by absolute positive multiples of $n\log n$, both over all convex bodies and over centrally symmetric convex bodies.
rows.explanation: States matching upper and lower bounds of order n log n for the translative and lattice covering-density suprema, over all and over centrally symmetric bodies. Its lower bound contains the main theorem of the translative paper.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result gives an absolute constant $C>0$ such that every convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, admits a covering by translates along one full-rank lattice $L$ with density $|K|/\mathrm{covol}(L)\le Cn\log n$. The covering is exact, and no symmetry, boundary regularity, or volume normalization is assumed.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: every convex body in dimension n ≥ 2 is covered by translates along one lattice with density at most Cn log n.

rows.scope_quote: For $p>1$, $p\ne2$, the formalization bounds the least dimension needed to embed every $n$-point subset of real $L_p$ with distortion $D$. For each fixed $D>1$, there is a constant $C=C(p,D)$ such that this dimension lies between $\log n/\log(1+2D)$ and $\exp(C(\log n)^{\gamma(p)})$ for every $n\ge2$, where $\gamma(p)=2-p$ for $p<2$ and $1-2/p$ for $p>2$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: for p > 1, p ≠ 2 and fixed distortion D > 1, the least embedding dimension for n-point subsets of L_p is at most exp(C(log n)^{γ(p)}), with the stated lower bound and the distortion-one case.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized counterexample is an explicit homogeneous polynomial of degree $20$ in $23$ real variables. It is hyperbolic, but its closed hyperbolicity cone cannot be represented as the positive-semidefinite region of any finite real symmetric linear matrix pencil, in any positive matrix size.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: an explicit degree-20 hyperbolic polynomial in 23 variables whose hyperbolicity cone is not spectrahedral. The semidefinite-lift questions of the family's later papers are not part of the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result proves the sharp bound $9/(8\pi)$ for every positive dimension and every positive number of labelled cells, allowing empty cells and arbitrary masses. In dimension at least two with at least three cells, three planar sectors of angle $120^\circ$, extended in orthogonal directions, attain equality.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: the sharp bound 9/(8π) for the sum of squared Gaussian first moments over every partition, in every dimension, with the propeller attaining it. The Gaussian-maxima and kernel-clustering consequences are not included.

rows.scope_quote: For every finite family of vectors in the unit ball of $\mathbb R^d$, signs can be chosen so that every prefix in the prescribed order has norm at most $C\sqrt d$. When the vector sum is zero, a permutation makes every unsigned prefix satisfy the same bound.
rows.explanation: States both main theorems: signed prefixes of norm at most C√d in a prescribed order, and, for zero-sum families, a reordering with every prefix of norm at most C√d.

rows.scope_quote: A companion gives one universal doubling constant such that every infinite-dimensional real Banach space contains a compact doubling subset with no bi-Lipschitz embedding into any finite-dimensional normed space.
rows.explanation: States the paper's Banach-space corollary (Section 7): every infinite-dimensional real Banach space contains a compact doubling subset, with one universal doubling bound, that embeds bi-Lipschitzly into no finite-dimensional normed space.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result gives a doubling subset of real $\ell_2$, with doubling constant at most $76800$, that admits no bi-Lipschitz embedding into any finite-dimensional Euclidean space at any finite distortion.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: one subset of ℓ2 with doubling constant at most 76800 that admits no bi-Lipschitz embedding into any Euclidean space.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization gives two lower-bound constructions for the $\ell_1$ distortion of ordinary edit distance on binary words. For every sufficiently large length cap $d$, each construction supplies a finite set of at least two binary words of one common length at most $d$ whose least $\ell_1$ distortion is at least $\exp(c\sqrt{\log d\,\log\log d})$ for an absolute $c>0$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the tree-constructions paper: for every large length cap d, a set of binary words of one common length with ℓ1 distortion at least exp(c√(log d log log d)). The paper's binary conversion and upper embedding are outside it.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization determines the exponential scale of the least $\ell_1$ distortion of unit-cost edit distance on strings of length at most $d$. For every sufficiently large $d$, uniformly over finite alphabets with at least two symbols, the distortion lies between $\exp(c\sqrt{\log d\,\log\log d})$ and $\exp(C\sqrt{\log d\,\log\log d})$ for absolute constants $c,C>0$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: the least ℓ1 distortion of edit distance on strings of length at most d lies between exp(c√(log d log log d)) and exp(C√(log d log log d)), uniformly over finite alphabets.

rows.scope_quote: It also gives a finite histogram embedding with distortion at most $\exp(C\sqrt{\log d\,\log\log d})$ for all strings of length at most $d$, uniformly over finite alphabets, including the empty string. Thus the lower and upper exponential scales agree up to absolute constants.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the finite-circle paper: finite-circle lower-bound witnesses and a histogram embedding together give matching exponential scales for edit-distance distortion.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization gives two lower-bound constructions for the $\ell_1$ distortion of ordinary edit distance on binary words. For every sufficiently large length cap $d$, each construction supplies a finite set of at least two binary words of one common length at most $d$ whose least $\ell_1$ distortion is at least $\exp(c\sqrt{\log d\,\log\log d})$ for an absolute $c>0$.
rows.explanation: States the same binary lower bound as BinaryEditLower, the main theorem of the tree-constructions paper, in a separately written statement file.

rows.scope_quote: The linked aggregate includes the accompanying explicit angular covers and finite approximation theorems for ruled sets and radial sweeps. The affine extension of the directionwise conclusion to every nondegenerate tetrahedron is outside the selected regular-tetrahedron statements.
rows.explanation: The aggregate file states the main theorems of all four accompanying papers: the explicit angular cover of the tetrahedron with ε ≤ 1/2000 and remainder at most 2ε⁴, the ruled-set approximation, the regular-tetrahedron counterexamples and the radial-sweep approximation. The extension to every nondegenerate tetrahedron is outside it.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization approximates compact ruled families of line segments by finite cylinder covers with perpendicular-base area at most the integral projection cost plus any prescribed positive error. The selected results cover the stated $C^1$ hyperbolic differential condition, square-zero and nilpotent cases, physical rescalings, logarithmic and product-cell estimates, and singular cases. Compact label sets need not have regular boundary.
rows.explanation: States the ruled-set paper's approximation theorem: compact ruled families of segments are approximated by finite cylinder covers with base area at most the projection cost plus any error, under the stated differential and segment-length hypotheses.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization constructs finite covers of a regular tetrahedron by cylinders with compact triangular bases whose total area is strictly below that bound. For the explicit small parameter $\varepsilon$, the normalized area is $1/2-(13/6000)\varepsilon^2+O(\varepsilon^4)$, giving the strict saving.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem's explicit cover with an unspecified range of ε and an unspecified constant in the ε⁴ remainder, where the paper states ε ≤ 1/2000 and a remainder of at most 2ε⁴; the strict saving below half the minimum projection area is included. The aggregate CylinderCovering states the explicit version.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves hardness of approximating the minimum such set within any fixed constant factor. For every real factor $A\ge1$ and every language in NP, it constructs a polynomial-time gap reduction to unweighted directed graphs with the stated completeness and soundness separation. Thus a fixed-factor polynomial-time approximation would imply a polynomial-time algorithm for every NP language.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: for every factor A ≥ 1, a polynomial-time gap reduction from any NP language to directed feedback vertex set, so fixed-factor approximation would put NP in P.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization constructs a deterministic reduction from encoded $3$-SAT formulas to finite simple unweighted Min-UnCut instances with arbitrarily large fixed multiplicative gaps. For every integer $K\ge2$, satisfiable formulas give optimum at most the output threshold, while unsatisfiable formulas give optimum strictly greater than $K$ times that threshold. Runtime and output length are polynomial for each fixed $K$, establishing hardness for every fixed approximation factor greater than one.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: for every K ≥ 2, a polynomial-time reduction from 3SAT to Min-UnCut with multiplicative gap K. The 2CNF-deletion corollary is not part of the statement.

rows.scope_quote: For every fixed $\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}<\alpha\le1$, it gives a deterministic polynomial-time reduction from binary 3SAT to a strictly separated Max-Cut gap on finite simple unweighted graphs. The reduction includes the explicit positive integer scaling used in the gap statement.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem in reduction form: for every α above the Goemans–Williamson constant, a polynomial-time reduction from 3SAT to a separated Max-Cut gap on simple unweighted graphs, which is how NP-hardness of α-approximation is expressed.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result gives, for every fixed $0<\varepsilon,\delta<1/2$, a deterministic polynomial-time reduction from binary 3SAT to nonempty unweighted simple bipartite unique games. Satisfiable inputs have value at least $1-\varepsilon$ and unsatisfiable inputs have value at most $\delta$.
rows.explanation: States the paper's Unique Games theorem as a reduction: for fixed ε, δ in (0, 1/2), a deterministic polynomial-time reduction from 3SAT to translation unique games with completeness 1 − ε and soundness δ.

rows.scope_quote: For each integer $m\ge4$, a polynomial-time reduction from binary 3SAT produces simple unweighted graphs with cover density below $1/2+1/m$ on satisfiable inputs and above $1-1/m$ on unsatisfiable inputs. Consequently, any polynomial-time approximation with a fixed factor $1\le\alpha<2$ would give a polynomial-time decision algorithm for 3SAT. No assumption that $P\ne NP$ is built into the statement.
rows.explanation: States the explicit cover-gap reduction for each m ≥ 4 and its corollary that approximation within any fixed factor below 2 would decide 3SAT in polynomial time.

rows.scope_quote: The selected theorem asserts equality of the language classes. The paper's explicit compiler and numerical running-time bounds are not separately stated in this Comparator target.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem L = RL = BPL in an explicit machine model. Comparator treats twenty of the file's definitions as holes filled from OpenAI's library; eighteen of them, including L, RL and BPL, have library bodies matching the challenge file after whitespace normalisation, and the two head-movement helpers were not compared.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result gives one randomized algorithm for the complete zero-threshold winning set of every finite mean-payoff game with signed binary weights. It succeeds with probability at least $7/8$ and runs in quasipolynomial bit time on every random tape. Self-loops, parallel edges, and history-dependent strategies are allowed, and winning means a nonnegative liminf average payoff.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the randomised paper: a quasipolynomial randomised algorithm computing the full winning set of every finite mean-payoff game with success probability at least 7/8. The deterministic algorithm of the companion paper is outside this statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization checks that a specified two-step execution of Truffet's elimination procedure terminates with a feasible but nonoptimal output. It is a finite counterexample to that proposed optimization step.
rows.explanation: States a finite counterexample to a variable-selection rule in Truffet's proposed elimination procedure, discussed in the randomised paper's comparison section. It is a side result, not a headline theorem.

rows.scope_quote: For every fixed rational $0<\delta<1$, a deterministic polynomial-time reduction from binary 3SAT produces a nonempty unweighted game of value exactly $1$ on satisfiable inputs and at most $\delta$ on unsatisfiable inputs. Each constraint projection has exactly two preimages for each output label. The alphabet depends only on $\delta$, and the runtime is measured in the original input bit length.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: for every rational δ in (0, 1), a polynomial-time reduction from 3SAT to 2-to-1 games with perfect completeness and soundness δ. The paper's corollaries are not part of the statement.

rows.scope_quote: For every fixed $0<\delta<1/3$, a deterministic polynomial-time reduction maps binary 3SAT formulas to nonempty finite simple graphs. Satisfiable formulas produce three-colorable graphs; unsatisfiable formulas produce graphs whose largest independent set has fewer than $\delta$ times the number of vertices.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: for fixed δ in (0, 1/3), a polynomial-time reduction from 3SAT producing three-colourable graphs from satisfiable formulas and graphs with no independent set of δ times the vertex count from unsatisfiable ones. The colouring corollary is not part of the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result gives the unconditional bound $\omega(F)<2.371054886006746$ for every field $F$, including finite fields and fields of positive characteristic. The exponent counts additions, subtractions, and multiplications in finite division-free arithmetic programs, with arbitrary positive exponent slack. No numerical inequalities remain as hypotheses.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the staggered-extraction paper: ω_F < 2.371054886006746 over every field F, with no numerical hypotheses left.

rows.scope_quote: The square bound implies the paper's weaker $2.258$ headline bound.
rows.explanation: States ω(C) ≤ 9/4, α > 0.465 and the rectangular bound at 0.709. Since 9/4 < 2.258, this implies all three bounds of the main theorem; the 9/4 bound itself is the subject of a later family paper that the note does not link.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves a cubic lower bound for both exact and border determinantal representations of the complex $m\times m$ permanent. For $m\ge1408$, every affine-linear determinant representation of size $n$, including coefficientwise limits, satisfies $n\ge m^3/(5529600e)$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem with its explicit constants: for m ≥ 1408, every exact or border determinantal representation of the m × m permanent has size at least m³/(5529600e).

rows.scope_quote: A general supporting theorem applies to a polynomial in $d\ge2$ variables whose first nonzero homogeneous Taylor term has degree $r\ge2$ and no nonzero singular zero. Its exact and border determinantal sizes are at least $(r-1)(d-1)/(4e)$.
rows.explanation: States the general supporting theorem behind the permanent bound: determinantal size at least (r − 1)(d − 1)/(4e) for a polynomial whose initial form has degree r and no nonzero singular zero.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves an $O((\log(k+1))^2)$ competitive ratio for randomized $k$-server against oblivious finite request sequences. For every $k\ge2$, every metric space containing at least $k+1$ points, and every initial configuration, one policy works for all request sequences, including in infinite and unbounded spaces.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: an O(log²(k + 1)) competitive randomised k-server policy on every metric space with at least k + 1 points. Nine definitions, including the statement MainStatement, are Comparator holes; the library's MainStatement has the same body as the challenge file's.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization constructs one uniform randomized bit algorithm for $k$-server on finite rational metrics, for $2\le k<n$. Its expected movement on every oblivious finite request sequence is at most an absolute multiple of $(\log(k+1))^2$ times the offline optimum, plus a finite instance-dependent additive constant.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the uniform-computation paper: one randomised bit algorithm on finite rational metrics achieving the squared-logarithmic bound, with polynomial preprocessing and per-request time.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves a one-sample matroid prophet inequality with expected reward at least $2^{-310}$ times the expected offline optimum. Each element has one independent sample paired with an identically distributed nonnegative online value, and all coordinates are independent. The rule and finite seed law depend only on the labeled matroid; choices are irrevocable and feasible after every prefix. The arrival order may depend measurably on all samples, values, and the seed, and only the offline optimum must be integrable.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem with the paper's constant: a one-sample matroid prophet inequality with reward at least 2^{-310} times the expected offline optimum against an adversary choosing the arrival order.

rows.scope_quote: A supporting hidden-vector selection result for fixed nonnegative matroid weights gives expected worst-order reward at least $2^{-293}$ times the optimum, again with a finite seed law and prefix feasibility.
rows.explanation: States the supporting hidden-vector selection result for fixed matroid weights (worst-order reward at least 2^{-293} times the optimum), not the prophet inequality itself.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result gives one polynomial-time Boolean language whose exact depth-three OR–AND–OR circuit size eventually exceeds $2^{A\sqrt n}$ for every fixed $A>0$. The language and its polynomial-time algorithm are fixed before $A$ is chosen, while circuits may vary with the input length. Gates have unrestricted finite fan-in and sharing, with free input negations and constants. The result does not assert a fixed exponent $n^{1/2+\varepsilon}$ or a lower bound for unrestricted depth.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: one polynomial-time language whose depth-three circuit size eventually exceeds 2^{A√n} for every fixed A > 0.

rows.scope_quote: It retains the earlier coefficient-eight entropy bound and the deterministic counting approximations with factors $512^n$ for loopless graphs and $2^{18n}$ with singleton loops.
rows.explanation: States the paper's deterministic approximate counting theorem: a polynomial-time algorithm returning A with N(G)/512^n ≤ A ≤ N(G) for loopless graphs.

rows.scope_quote: It retains the earlier coefficient-eight entropy bound and the deterministic counting approximations with factors $512^n$ for loopless graphs and $2^{18n}$ with singleton loops.
rows.explanation: States the earlier nonlinear entropy bound F − H ≤ 8m(1 − e^{−F/m}), a theorem in Section 12 of the paper that the note says is retained, rather than the headline pointwise bound with coefficient 2 − 2/m. Whether the headline bound implies it, which would make it a weaker form, was not settled here.

rows.scope_quote: For feasible edge marginals $x$ of perfect matchings in a loopless multigraph on $2m$ vertices, let $F(x)=-\sum_e x_e\log x_e$, $B(x)=-\sum_e(1-x_e)\log(1-x_e)$, and let $H(x)$ be the maximum entropy of a matching law with those marginals. The formalization proves $F(x)-(2-2/m)B(x)\le H(x)\le F(x)$ for $m\ge1$, including boundary points of the polytope.
rows.explanation: States the paper's pointwise entropy theorem F − (2 − 2/m)B ≤ H ≤ F for every point of the perfect matching polytope, including boundary points.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization gives a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for counting perfect matchings in every finite simple undirected graph. For rational $0<\varepsilon<1$ and $0<\delta<1/2$, it returns a nonnegative rational estimate with relative error at most $\varepsilon$ with probability at least $1-\delta$. If the graph has no perfect matching, every execution returns zero.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: a fully polynomial randomised approximation scheme for the number of perfect matchings of every finite simple graph.

rows.scope_quote: It retains the earlier coefficient-eight entropy bound and the deterministic counting approximations with factors $512^n$ for loopless graphs and $2^{18n}$ with singleton loops.
rows.explanation: States the paper's extension of deterministic counting to graphs with singleton loops, with factor 2^{18n} (a proposition in Section 13), rather than a headline theorem.

rows.scope_quote: A further statement identifies the exact face obtained by expanding a degree-three vertex into a triangle and shows that minimal faces are carried to minimal faces by the expansion. The paper's sharp global face-dimension bound is not part of that selected statement.
rows.explanation: States a lemma on faces of the perfect matching polytope under triangle expansion of a degree-three vertex. The paper's global face-dimension bound is outside it.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result gives a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for the number of common bases of two equal-rank matroids on an enumerated finite ground set, using independence oracles. For rational $0<\varepsilon,\delta<1$, the nonnegative rational output has relative error at most $\varepsilon$ with probability at least $1-\delta$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: an FPRAS, using independence oracles, for the number of common bases of two equal-rank matroids. The integer-polymatroid version of the family's later paper is not part of the statement.

rows.scope_quote: It also gives a sampler with a fixed polynomial time bound on every execution whose total-variation error is at most $2^{-k}$ for requested precision $k\ge1$. The same Comparator file includes the companion approximation scheme for counting tables with individual cell bounds.
rows.explanation: The file states the main theorems of both papers: exact uniform sampling of contingency tables with arbitrary margins in polynomial expected bit time with a bounded-time approximate sampler, and the FPRAS for cell-bounded tables.

rows.scope_quote: The selected theorem states this universal hitting property. The paper's deterministic polynomial bit-construction bound and matrix-dimension bound $O(ns^2)$ are not separately asserted in it.
rows.explanation: States the hitting property of the paper's explicit matrix tuple for all nonzero formulas of bounded size over fields of characteristic zero. The main theorem's polynomial-time construction and its dimension and bit-length bounds are not asserted.

rows.scope_quote: Given the number of variables and a formula-size bound, one deterministic polynomial-time machine outputs rational matrix tuples of a common positive dimension. Every admissible nonzero formula within the size bound evaluates to an invertible matrix on some listed tuple. The matrix dimension, complete binary output length, and running time are all polynomially bounded.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the rational-formula paper: one deterministic polynomial-time machine outputs hitting lists of rational matrix tuples for formulas with inverse gates, with polynomial dimension, output length and running time.

rows.scope_quote: Along a sequence of instance sizes $n\to\infty$, the ratio of the integral optimum to the positive relaxation optimum is at least $c\sqrt{\log n}/(\log\log n)^3$ for one absolute $c>0$. Every unordered pair has unit demand, and the relaxation uses squared Euclidean distances satisfying the triangle inequalities. The result is an existential sequence, not a bound for every size or a computational hardness theorem.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: a sequence of uniform sparsest-cut instances whose Goemans–Linial integrality gap is at least c√(log n)/(log log n)³. The hardness result of the family's other paper is not part of the statement.

rows.scope_quote: For every integer $c\ge0$, there are an integer $B$ and a rational instance with $5B$ items whose individual-copy and size-type configuration-LP values both equal $B$, but whose integral optimum is greater than $B+c$. Distinguishing a packing in $B$ bins from the absence of one in $B+c$ bins is NP-hard for each fixed $c$. A deterministic polynomial-time algorithm with a fixed absolute additive allowance exists exactly when $P=NP$; under that equality, an optimal algorithm is constructed.
rows.explanation: States the paper's three headline statements: unbounded configuration-LP gaps, NP-hardness of distinguishing B from B + c bins, and the equivalence of a constant-additive polynomial-time algorithm with P = NP.

rows.scope_quote: For Boolean functions this includes the Courtade–Kumar inequality $I(f(X);Y)\le1-h_2(\varepsilon)$ in bits at crossover probability $0\le\varepsilon\le1/2$, where $h_2$ is binary entropy. A coordinate and its complement attain equality.
rows.explanation: States the Courtade–Kumar inequality I(f(X);Y) ≤ 1 − h₂(ε) for Boolean functions with attainment by a coordinate, which the paper obtains as the Boolean specialisation of its sharp soft-channel contraction theorem.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves sharp contraction of the information carried by a binary channel under independent symmetric noise on a uniform discrete cube. At each fixed initial information level, a noisy coordinate channel attains the maximum retained information. It also proves the refined Boolean bound that accounts for output bias, with strict improvement for nonconstant biased outputs at nonzero noise correlation, and the selected mean-dependent entropy-production inequality.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem (sharp contraction of binary-channel information under symmetric noise) with the bias-refined Boolean corollary and the selected entropy-production inequality.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization gives a randomized $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximation for unit-cost edit distance between explicitly stored integer strings, for every fixed rational $0<\varepsilon<1$. Its estimate is at least the true distance and at most $(1+\varepsilon)$ times it with probability at least $2/3$; equal strings return zero on every execution.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem in an explicit machine model: a randomised (1 + ε)-approximation of edit distance with expected work (N + 2)^{1+η} for every η > 0, for integer symbols bounded by a polynomial in N, which corresponds to the paper's logarithmic-word RAM.

rows.scope_quote: More quantitatively, along sequences with $q^3\log n\to\infty$, the required number of samples is at least $n^{c\log(q^3\log n)}$ eventually for every fixed $0<c<1/(4\log2)$. All logarithms are natural.
rows.explanation: States both headline theorems: the quantitative sample lower bound n^{c log(q³ log n)} and superpolynomial decay of the one-trace total-variation distance, hence superpolynomial sample complexity. The upper-bound algorithms of the family's later papers are not part of it.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization gives a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for scheduling nonempty collections of unit-length jobs with arbitrary acyclic precedence constraints on three identical parallel machines. It constructs a schedule of minimum makespan and decides exactly whether a valid specified deadline can be met. The algorithm is one fixed finite machine, and its running time is bounded by a polynomial in the binary input length.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm computing a minimum-makespan schedule for unit jobs with precedence constraints on three identical machines.

rows.scope_quote: The linked final approximation result applies to arbitrary finite rational metrics. For one absolute $\sigma>0$, a polynomial-time fair-bit algorithm always returns a feasible solution, has expected cost at most $(2-\sigma)\mathrm{OPT}$, and attains the same factor with arbitrarily high polynomial confidence.
rows.explanation: States the paper's global application theorem: for one absolute σ > 0, a randomised polynomial-time k-median algorithm with expected cost at most (2 − σ)OPT on finite rational metrics.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization gives an exact-budget recovery algorithm for metric $k$-median on the stated polynomially bounded integral metrics. Suppose a supplied anchor represents all but logarithmically many comparison clusters by distinct proxies, with total proxy cost at most the comparison cost plus a sufficiently small relative error. The algorithm always opens at most $k$ facilities and, with any requested confidence, attains a $(1+2/e+\varepsilon)$ factor relative to those comparison centers in polynomial time.
rows.explanation: States the paper's refined recovery theorem: from an anchor with accurate distinct cluster proxies, an exact-budget algorithm attaining factor 1 + 2/e + ε on polynomially bounded integral metrics.

rows.scope_quote: Assuming $P\ne NP$, it also proves that the infimum of all polynomial-time approximation factors in this model is exactly $1+2/e$.
rows.explanation: States the paper's threshold corollary: assuming P ≠ NP, the infimum of polynomial-time approximation factors is exactly 1 + 2/e. It combines the main algorithm with a hardness bound; attainment is not asserted.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization gives, for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, a deterministic polynomial-time $(1+2/e+\varepsilon)$-approximation for metric $k$-median on finite rational metrics with specified candidate facilities. Every output is a nonempty subset of the candidate facilities and opens at most $k$ of them.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the threshold paper: a deterministic polynomial-time (1 + 2/e + ε)-approximation for metric k-median with candidate facilities.

rows.scope_quote: These selected statements give superpolynomial growth. They do not state the paper's exponential bound for every fixed positive shift.
rows.explanation: States that exact affine semidefinite lifts of the perfect-matching polytope need size above n^C for every C, a superpolynomial form of the paper's exponential lift bound. The exponential bound for positively shifted matrices is not stated.

rows.scope_quote: These selected statements give superpolynomial growth. They do not state the paper's exponential bound for every fixed positive shift.
rows.explanation: States that the PSD rank of the perfect-matching slack matrix eventually exceeds n^C for every C, a superpolynomial form of the paper's exponential bounds. The exponential bound for positively shifted matrices is not stated.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result proves the average-sensitivity bound $8d\sqrt n$ for every Boolean threshold function defined by a real multilinear polynomial of degree at most $d$ on the $n$-dimensional cube. The sign convention assigns value $1$ at zero. This establishes the stated asymptotic bound, rather than the separate conjecture identifying exact extremizers.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem with its constant: average sensitivity at most 8d√n for every degree-d polynomial threshold function on the n-cube, with sign 1 at zero.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result gives one deterministic polynomial-time algorithm whose output is a common superstring of length at most twice the unrestricted optimum. It applies to every finite list of explicitly encoded strings, with running time measured in input bits and the approximation ratio measured in symbol length.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm returning a common superstring of length at most twice the optimum.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization gives a family of one-way nondeterministic automata with $h+3$ states whose languages require exponentially many states for two-way deterministic recognition. For every $h\ge2$, a deterministic recognizer with $s$ states satisfies $2^{\lfloor(h-2)/31\rfloor}\le4(s+2)^2$ under both acceptance conventions considered in the paper; one convention has the sharper factor $4(s+1)^2$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the liveness paper: one-way nondeterministic automata with h + 3 states whose languages need exponentially many states for two-way deterministic recognition, with the explicit bound.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization gives, for every $n\ge4$, an explicit $n$-state automaton whose complement requires at least $\tfrac12 2^{\lfloor(n-4)/127\rfloor}-1$ states.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem with its explicit bound: for every n ≥ 4, an n-state two-way nondeterministic automaton whose complement needs at least ½·2^{⌊(n−4)/127⌋} − 1 states.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization gives, for every $n\ge4$, an explicit $n$-state automaton whose complement requires at least $\tfrac12 2^{\lfloor(n-4)/127\rfloor}-1$ states. For the same family of relational languages and every $n\ge131$, every equivalent deterministic two-way automaton requires at least $\tfrac12 2^{\lfloor(n-4)/127\rfloor}$ states.
rows.explanation: States the main complementation bound together with the paper's determinisation corollary for the same witness, with the explicit constant ½ and threshold n ≥ 131 where the corollary states unspecified constants.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result gives exact discrete Fourier transforms with arbitrarily small normalized circuit cost along an unbounded sequence of lengths. For every $c>0$ and every cutoff $N_0\ge2$, some $n\ge N_0$ has a circuit computing the unnormalized DFT with fewer than $cn\log_2 n$ gates. Addition, subtraction, and multiplication by a predetermined complex scalar each cost one gate; diagonal scalings are charged. The result is subsequential, with no all-length, bounded-coefficient, conditioning, or bit-complexity claim.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: along an unbounded sequence of lengths, exact DFT circuits with fewer than cn log₂ n gates for every c > 0.

rows.scope_quote: A separate uniform formalization gives fixed deterministic programs for every positive length $n$, computing the canonical discrete Fourier transform and the full convolution of two length-$n$ complex vectors exactly. Their work is $O(n(\log n)^{1-10^{-13}})=o(n\log n)$, including root-order selection and scalar preparation. The chosen root of unity is supplied; the model permits exact complex arithmetic and unrestricted coefficients, while integer values and indices remain polynomially bounded in $n$.
rows.explanation: States the power-saving paper's main theorem with its corollaries: one fixed program computing the DFT at every length, and exact convolution, in O(n(log n)^{1−10^{-13}}) operations.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves the simple undirected case: for $n\ge4$, the lazy chain that proposes switches on four vertices has total-variation mixing time at distance $1/4$ at most $2n^8$. It also proves switch connectivity, the stated exponential total-variation bound, and a spectral gap of at least $1/(24n^2\binom n4)$ when more than one graph realizes the degree sequence.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: the switch chain mixes in at most 2n⁸ steps for every graphical degree sequence, with connectivity and the spectral-gap bound. The exact sampling corollary is outside the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result disproves a universal quadratic bound of block sensitivity by sensitivity for total Boolean functions. For every integer $d\ge1$, it constructs a nonconstant function with $\mathrm{bs}(f)/s(f)^2\ge2^d/(4(d+2)^2)$, making the ratio unbounded. The formalization also gives a fixed exponent $\alpha>2$ and a sequence with $s(f)^\alpha\le\mathrm{bs}(f,0)$ while the latter tends to infinity; here $\mathrm{bs}(f,0)$ is block sensitivity at the all-zero input.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem that bs(f)/s(f)² is unbounded, with the explicit ratio 2^d/(4(d + 2)²), together with a polynomial separation of exponent above 2 at the all-zero input.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization gives the paper's parity-lift graph construction for every Weisfeiler–Leman dimension $k\ge4$, under both joint and separate conventions. From a finite choice system it constructs two equal-size uncolored graphs that are Weisfeiler–Leman equivalent exactly when the system has no successful compatible choice. The same equivalence holds for the pure variant.
rows.explanation: States the paper's parity-reduction theorem for every dimension k ≥ 4 under both conventions. The ETH-conditional running-time consequence is outside the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves EXPTIME-completeness of deciding joint-update $k$-dimensional Weisfeiler–Leman equivalence when $k\ge2$ is part of the input in binary and the graphs are encoded by explicit adjacency matrices. It proves both the general result and the restriction to connected simple uncolored graphs of equal positive order and maximum degree at most three. Completeness uses polynomial-time many-one reductions.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: EXPTIME-completeness of variable-dimension Weisfeiler–Leman equivalence, in general and on connected subcubic graphs.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves that deciding whether Weisfeiler–Leman refinement of a supplied dimension identifies a graph is EXPTIME-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions. The input is a nonempty finite simple uncolored graph encoded by its adjacency matrix together with a positive binary-encoded dimension. Identification quantifies over every comparison graph, and the statement includes both the exponential-time upper bound and hardness.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: deciding whether Weisfeiler–Leman refinement of a given dimension identifies a graph is EXPTIME-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves an unconditional deterministic time lower bound for deciding $k$-dimensional Weisfeiler–Leman equivalence. For every sufficiently large fixed $k$, every deciding algorithm in the stated multitape Turing-machine or sequential logarithmic-word RAM model requires at least $n^{ck}$ worst-case time for all sufficiently large graph orders $n$, for one absolute $c>0$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: an unconditional n^{ck} deterministic time lower bound for deciding k-dimensional Weisfeiler–Leman equivalence, for all large fixed k.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves that every regular language over a finite alphabet has a generalized regular expression over that same alphabet of star height at most three. Complements are taken in the same free monoid. This is the paper's uniform bound.
rows.explanation: States the bound of three, the main theorem of the newest accompanying paper; it implies the bounds of four and thirteen that are the main theorems of the other two accompanying papers.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves that, over every characteristic-zero field, syntactically homogeneous depth-five $\Sigma\Pi\Sigma\Pi\Sigma$ circuits computing this polynomial require at least $n^{\sqrt n/400}$ gates for all sufficiently large $n$, with a threshold independent of the field. Arbitrary bottom support, finite fan-in and fan-out, and sharing are allowed.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem with the explicit exponent √n/400 over every field of characteristic zero, together with the upper bound n^{√n+4}.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization gives two-fifths-power space simulation of a fixed deterministic machine with one writable tape and finitely many read-only input heads. Heads move at most one cell per step, initial contents are independent of the time bound, and contents and input symbols must be accessible in polylogarithmic space. Given a binary time cap $T\ge2$, the simulator returns the source's finite-control outcome and halting flag using $O(T^{2/5}(\log(T+2))^C)$ space.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: a one-tape machine running for time T is simulated in O(T^{2/5} polylog T) space, in a time-capped form and a form without a cap. Multitape and hierarchy consequences are outside it.

rows.scope_quote: For potentials with $V(0)=0$, $\nabla V(0)=0$, and $I\le\nabla^2V\le2I$, the least worst-case query budget achieving total-variation error at most $1/10$ is at most $C_\varepsilon d^\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, and at least $c\log d$ eventually. Hence the infimal polynomial exponent is zero.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: for well-conditioned log-concave sampling, the query complexity is at most C_ε d^ε for every ε > 0 and at least c log d, so the polynomial exponent is zero.

rows.scope_quote: For a law of finite relative entropy with respect to a uniform cell law in sufficiently large dimension, the regularization procedure terminates almost surely in regular cells. Its expected depth and number of attempts are finite, with at most twice one plus the expected depth in expectation; the remaining relative entropy plus $(\log 2)n/4$ times the expected depth is at most the initial relative entropy plus $2/e$.
rows.explanation: States a regularisation lemma of the localisation paper: from finite relative entropy the procedure ends almost surely in regular cells with controlled expected depth. It supports the paper's localisation theorem rather than being a headline result.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization controls information gained from exact Gaussian observations of a spherical image of the uniform cube. Under the stated entropy and size conditions, repeated localization over $t$ observation blocks produces nested disclosures with mutual information at most $C(n+1)t$ and expected final localization level at most $Ct$. The selected estimates include inverse-volume control, kernel coercivity, and drift for the actual observation rows.
rows.explanation: States the localisation paper's main theorem on repeated localisation over t observation blocks (mutual information at most C(n + 1)t, expected final level at most Ct) with its selected estimates. The paper's regression lower bounds are not part of the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The paper compares fresh Gaussian observations with observations coupled to information already held in memory. The formalization covers mixed-moment and actual-row estimates, critical-radius, one-level, and two-label comparisons, and conditional-information bounds across a block of observations. For sufficiently large dimension $d$, the relevant entropy bounds of order $d^2$ bound the information in the fresh experiment by that in the coupled experiment plus a term of order $d$; the associated block information increase also has order $d$.
rows.explanation: States the replacement paper's mixed-moment and critical-radius comparison theorems with the related block estimates. The paper's streaming consequence is outside the selection.

rows.scope_quote: The linked supporting results include inverse Gram-matrix moments, exact-projection densities, regularization bounds, and sphere- and cube-prior block estimates.
rows.explanation: Bundles the supporting estimates the note lists (Gram-matrix moments, densities, cube-prior block bounds) with the lower bound T ≥ cd log(1/ε) for memory at most d² under an every-signal guarantee, one case of the main theorem, and a uniform-sphere success bound for general memory. Whether that bound gives the main theorem for every fixed A was not settled here.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves that, for every fixed $A>0$, there is $c_A>0$ such that, in sufficiently large dimension, a learner retaining at most $Ad^2$ bits between observations needs at least $c_A d\log(1/\varepsilon)$ observations to attain angular error at most $\varepsilon$ with probability at least $2/3$ for a uniformly random unit signal, for $0<\varepsilon\le1/10$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem (for each fixed A, memory at most Ad² bits forces c_A d log(1/ε) observations) and the subquadratic-memory corollary with a universal constant, including success guaranteed for every signal.

rows.scope_quote: For a learner using $M(d)=o(d^2)$ bits of memory, the resulting bound says that, for sufficiently large $d$ and $0<\varepsilon\le1/10$, success probability at least $2/3$ under the uniform unit-sphere prior requires $T\ge c d\log(1/\varepsilon)$ observations, where $c>0$ is universal. The formalized streaming result uses the $2/3$ threshold; the stronger $3/5$ variant is outside this scope.
rows.explanation: States the replica paper's equal-label identity and information bounds together with its uniform-prior sample lower bound T ≥ cd log(1/ε) for memory o(d²) at success probability 2/3, the threshold of the paper's theorem.

rows.scope_quote: The paper uses projection moments and domination by positive spherical caps to bound the information carried by exact Gaussian observations of an unknown unit vector. The formalization covers integrated frame and sphere moments, cap domination, Riesz-density estimates with fixed offsets, and bounds valid at every radius. It also covers probability bounds for finite-memory learners at a fixed stopping time and after summing over stopping times.
rows.explanation: States the projection paper's moment, cap-domination and Riesz estimates together with finite-memory precision bounds for subquadratic and fixed-quadratic memory in a finite-kernel learner model, which contain the paper's finite-memory precision theorem.
