rows.scope_quote: The paper uses subspheres to bound the number of exact Gaussian observations needed to estimate a unit vector with limited memory. The formalization proves that, for $M(d)=o(d^2)$ bits of memory, sufficiently large $d$, and $0<\varepsilon\le1/10$, success probability at least $2/3$ under the uniform sphere prior, or for every unit signal, requires at least $2^{-16}d\log_2(1/\varepsilon)$ observations. Under the uniform prior, a lower bound of the same order with a universal positive constant holds at success probability $1/2$.
rows.explanation: States the subsphere paper's main theorem with its explicit constant (at least 2^{-16} d log₂(1/ε) observations for memory o(d²)) and the every-signal corollary.

rows.scope_quote: For the quintic Liénard system $x'=y-F(x)$, $y'=-x$, the formalized result proves that every real polynomial $F$ of degree at most five yields at most two limit cycles, and that some such $F$ yields exactly two. Limit cycles are isolated images of nonconstant periodic solutions. No sign, parity, hyperbolicity, or amplitude restriction is imposed.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: quintic Liénard systems have at most two limit cycles, and some have exactly two.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization constructs a smooth volume-preserving diffeomorphism of the three-torus with this property. It gives a real-valued cyclic vector whose integer iterates form an orthonormal basis of the entire mean-zero space, and an isometric identification under which the Koopman operator becomes multiplication by the coordinate function on the circle. The transformation is also ergodic.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: a smooth volume-preserving diffeomorphism of the three-torus with simple Lebesgue spectrum, given by a cyclic vector whose iterates form an orthonormal basis of the mean-zero space.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves this implication. For each $k\ge3$ and every $k$ measurable sets, the measure of their translated intersection tends to the product of their measures as all successive time gaps tend to infinity.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: every mixing invertible probability-preserving transformation is mixing of every order k ≥ 3. Four definitions, including mixing and mixing of order k, are Comparator holes; their library bodies match the challenge file.

rows.scope_quote: It also constructs a positive-area invariant ergodic hyperbolic component. That component splits into finitely many cyclic pieces on each of which the corresponding iterate is Bernoulli. No genericity assumption on the parameter is used.
rows.explanation: States the paper's corollary: a positive-area ergodic hyperbolic component splitting into finitely many cyclic Bernoulli pieces, rather than the entropy theorem itself.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves Sinai's positive-entropy conjecture for the standard sine map on the two-dimensional torus in the stronger form of a full positive parameter tail. For every sufficiently large parameter, normalized area has positive metric entropy, and a positive-area set has positive largest Lyapunov exponent with the stated derivative-growth limit.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: the standard map has positive metric entropy for every sufficiently large parameter.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves Sinai's positive-entropy conjecture for the standard sine map on the two-dimensional torus in the stronger form of a full positive parameter tail. For every sufficiently large parameter, normalized area has positive metric entropy, and a positive-area set has positive largest Lyapunov exponent with the stated derivative-growth limit.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem in its Lyapunov form: positive entropy and a positive-area set with positive largest Lyapunov exponent and the stated derivative growth, for all large parameters.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves $\dim_H\mu=\min\{1,h_{\mathrm{RW}}/\chi\}$ for the lower Hausdorff dimension of every finite real self-similar probability measure with positive weights and nonzero contraction ratios of absolute value below one. Here $h_{\mathrm{RW}}$ is the entropy rate of random affine compositions and $\chi$ is the corresponding Lyapunov exponent in the same logarithmic base. Ratios may be signed and unequal, and exact overlaps are allowed.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: the lower Hausdorff dimension of every self-similar measure on the line is min{1, h_RW/χ}, with signed unequal ratios and exact overlaps allowed.

rows.scope_quote: It also gives two consequences without exact overlaps: the usual entropy-over-Lyapunov formula for a common positive contraction ratio, and the attractor formula $\dim_H K=\min\{1,s\}$, where $s\ge0$ is the unique solution of $\sum_i|r_i|^s=1$. Absolute continuity is outside these statements.
rows.explanation: States two consequences of the main theorem without exact overlaps: the entropy-over-Lyapunov formula for a common contraction ratio and the attractor formula dim K = min{1, s}.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves this for every finite weakly reversible reaction network with positive constant reaction rates and every strictly positive initial state. A global forward solution exists, and one $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ bounds every concentration of every global forward solution between $\varepsilon$ and $\varepsilon^{-1}$ for all nonnegative times. The bound may depend on the network, rates, and initial state.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: global boundedness and persistence for every weakly reversible mass-action network with positive constant rates, with bounds depending on the network, rates and initial state. The uniform permanence of the family's later paper is not part of it.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves that the unit-speed billiard flow in every nondegenerate Euclidean triangle with at least one angle irrational relative to $\pi$ is ergodic for normalized area times uniform angular measure. It constructs the flow outside the null set of exceptional trajectories, proves uniqueness of the flight chain there, and establishes measure preservation and the flow law almost everywhere. No genericity or Diophantine condition on the irrational angle is assumed.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: the billiard flow in every triangle with an angle irrational relative to π is ergodic, with the flow constructed off a null set. The weak mixing of the family's later paper is not part of the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization gives a counterexample to the general $C^1$ self-map version: a noninvertible $C^1$ map on a compact smooth manifold without boundary has topological entropy zero, while its action on second real homology has a nonzero eigenvector with eigenvalue $2$. Thus the homological lower bound is strictly positive and fails for this map.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: a noninvertible C¹ self-map of the paper's compact manifold with zero topological entropy whose action on second real homology has eigenvalue 2.

rows.scope_quote: The linked statement gives finite entropy; the paper's stronger zero-entropy conclusion is outside this statement.
rows.explanation: States an ergodic system with finite entropy and no smooth positive-volume model, where the main theorem gives such a system with zero entropy.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized counterexample is a finite tile in $\mathbb Z^3$ that tiles but has no complement invariant under a finite-index subgroup. Its unit-cube thickening also tiles $\mathbb R^3$ almost everywhere but admits no fully periodic tiling, even with arbitrary real translation vectors. The result also establishes that dimension three is the least lattice dimension where this failure occurs.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: a finite tile in Z³ that tiles but admits no periodic tiling, with its cube thickening in R³, and minimality of dimension three.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized counterexample is the compact set of rank-one orthogonal projectors onto lines in $\mathbb R^4$, with the Frobenius metric. It lies in the nine-dimensional affine space of trace-one symmetric matrices, has diameter $\sqrt2$, and cannot be covered by ten arbitrary sets of smaller diameter.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: the rank-one projectors onto lines in R⁴ form a set of diameter √2 in a nine-dimensional space that cannot be covered by ten sets of smaller diameter.

rows.scope_quote: This disproves the ordinary chromatic form. The paper's fractional-chromatic strengthening and the Colin de Verdière consequence are outside this selected statement.
rows.explanation: States the ordinary-chromatic part of the paper's corollary disproving Hadwiger's conjecture (graphs with independence number at most two and h(G) < 26m/75 + 2/3 < m/2 ≤ χ(G)). The main theorem's matching bound and the fractional strengthening are outside the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves that there is one integer $C\ge1$ such that every finite nonempty simple graph $G$ satisfies $\chi_{\mathrm{list}}(G)\le C h(G)$, where $h(G)$ is the largest order of a clique minor. The constant is independent of the graph.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the list-colouring paper: one constant C with list chromatic number at most C times the Hadwiger number for every finite graph.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized results prove that five colors do not suffice and that seven colors do suffice. The lower bound applies to arbitrary colorings, with no measurability or continuity assumption; the upper bound includes every boundary point of the coloring regions.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem that the plane has no proper five-colouring, with arbitrary colour classes. The one Comparator hole, the definition of a proper colouring, has the same body in the library up to the names of bound variables.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized results prove that five colors do not suffice and that seven colors do suffice. The lower bound applies to arbitrary colorings, with no measurability or continuity assumption; the upper bound includes every boundary point of the coloring regions.
rows.explanation: States the classical upper bound χ(R²) ≤ 7, the upper half of the main theorem's displayed consequence 6 ≤ χ(R²) ≤ 7; the lower half is EuclideanFiveColor.

rows.scope_quote: The selected theorem is the reciprocal-sum consequence. The paper's quantitative upper bound for the largest progression-free subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is outside this statement.
rows.explanation: States the reciprocal-sum corollary (Erdős's conjecture), which the paper derives from its quasipolynomial bound for sets without k-term progressions. The bound itself is outside the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result gives an absolute threshold $K$ such that $W(r,k)>k^{k\lfloor\log_2 r\rfloor/100000}$ for all $k\ge K$ and $r\ge2$. It also establishes the associated growth limits, finiteness, and boundary values. The sharper intermediate estimates used in the paper are not part of the described formalization.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem with its constant: W(r, k) > k^{k⌊log₂ r⌋/100000} for all k above an absolute threshold and r ≥ 2.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization disproves this for the paper's fixed bipartite graph with $35$ vertices and $66$ edges: it constructs a nonempty finite simple host graph with $t(H,G)<t(K_2,G)^{66}$. The separate forcing-conjecture consequence in the paper is outside this statement.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: for the paper's bipartite graph with 35 vertices and 66 edges, a finite host graph with t(H, G) < t(K₂, G)^66. The amplification and forcing corollaries are outside the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves that every sufficiently large prime $q$ has a finite intersecting $(q+1)$-partite, $(q+1)$-uniform hypergraph with covering number $q+1$ and exactly $q+1$ nonisolated vertices in each part. Thus the conjecture fails even with equal part sizes. The prime threshold is existential.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the balanced paper: for every large prime q, an intersecting (q + 1)-partite (q + 1)-uniform hypergraph with equal parts and covering number q + 1.

rows.scope_quote: The ranks have the form $r=p^n+1$: one fixed prime $p\equiv2\pmod3$ works for all sufficiently large prime degrees $n$, and a second result covers every sufficiently large such prime $p$ and every sufficiently large odd $n$, with the degree threshold allowed to depend on $p$. Infinitely many ranks occur. Equal part sizes and numerical thresholds are not asserted.
rows.explanation: States counterexamples of rank p^n + 1 for one fixed prime p ≡ 2 (mod 3) and all large prime degrees n, whereas the main theorem covers every large such prime and every large odd degree; the latter is RyserOddExtensions.

rows.scope_quote: The ranks have the form $r=p^n+1$: one fixed prime $p\equiv2\pmod3$ works for all sufficiently large prime degrees $n$, and a second result covers every sufficiently large such prime $p$ and every sufficiently large odd $n$, with the degree threshold allowed to depend on $p$. Infinitely many ranks occur. Equal part sizes and numerical thresholds are not asserted.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: for every sufficiently large prime p ≡ 2 (mod 3) and every sufficiently large odd n, an intersecting (p^n + 1)-partite hypergraph with ν = 1 and τ = r, giving infinitely many ranks.

rows.scope_quote: Zarankiewicz's crossing-number conjecture predicts $\mathrm{cr}(K_{m,n})=\lfloor m/2\rfloor\lfloor(m-1)/2\rfloor\lfloor n/2\rfloor\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor$. The formalized result proves this equality for every positive $m,n$ and constructs a drawing attaining it.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: Zarankiewicz's formula for the crossing number of K_{m,n} for all positive m, n, with a drawing attaining it.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result proves Hill's proposed formula for the crossing number of the complete graph: for every $n\ge3$, $\mathrm{cr}(K_n)=\frac14\lfloor n/2\rfloor\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\lfloor(n-3)/2\rfloor$. It proves the lower bound and constructs a matching two-page drawing.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: Hill's formula for the crossing number of K_n for every n ≥ 3, with the lower bound and a matching drawing.

rows.scope_quote: For each fixed $s>0$, the largest possible fraction of ordered distinct pairs $(x,y)$ whose distance from the pin $x$ occurs at least $n^s$ times tends to zero as the set size $n$ grows. Consequently, for every $\varepsilon>0$, the fraction of pins determining fewer than $n^{1-\varepsilon}$ distances tends uniformly to zero.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem (pins with many repeated distances are rare) and its corollary on pins determining few distances.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves that there are absolute constants $C>0$ and $1\le\beta<4/3$ such that every finite planar point set of size $n$ determines at most $Cn^\beta$ unordered unit-distance pairs. The same constants work for every $n$, giving a fixed power improvement over the classical exponent $4/3$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: absolute constants C and β < 4/3 with at most Cn^β unit distances among n points in the plane.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves that every order isomorphism between Bruhat intervals in arbitrary Coxeter systems preserves the corresponding equal-parameter Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial. The two intervals may come from different Coxeter systems.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: an order isomorphism between Bruhat intervals, possibly in different Coxeter systems, preserves the Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves this over $\mathbb N[q]$. It constructs an explicit elementary-basis expansion indexed by the graph's permitted nondescent permutations, with each term weighted by a nonnegative power of $q$ determined by its graph inversions. The expansion holds for every finite number of color variables.
rows.explanation: States elementary positivity over N[q] with the permutation-indexed expansion. The file has no theorem: Comparator checks the type of one definition hole, whose type is the witness structure carrying the expansion. That the partition is produced by a deterministic procedure, as the main theorem states, is not part of the checked type.

rows.scope_quote:
It proves
$r(5,t)=t^4/(\log t)^{3+o(1)}$ as $t\to\infty$.
For every $\varepsilon>0$, the lower bound $t^4/(\log t)^{3+\varepsilon}$ holds eventually, while the upper bound is $Ct^4/(\log t)^3$ for an absolute $C>0$. The corresponding logarithmic exponent converges to three along all natural values of $t$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: r(5, t) = t⁴/(log t)^{3+o(1)}, with upper bound Ct⁴/(log t)³.

rows.scope_quote:
It proves
$r(s,t)=t^{s-1}/(\log t)^{s-2+o(1)}$ as $t\to\infty$.
More explicitly, for each $\varepsilon>0$ the lower bound $t^{s-1}/(\log t)^{s-2+\varepsilon}$ holds eventually, while the upper bound is $C_s t^{s-1}/(\log t)^{s-2}$. The logarithmic exponent limit is taken along all natural values of $t$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: for every fixed s ≥ 6, r(s, t) = t^{s−1}/(log t)^{s−2+o(1)}, with upper bound C_s t^{s−1}/(log t)^{s−2}.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization gives the tensor-field classification for full-affine-span configurations, covers singleton and affine-span reductions, and proves that every Ramsey configuration is cospherical.
rows.explanation: States the main classification theorem for configurations of full affine span, with the singleton and affine-span reductions.

rows.scope_quote: It also proves that every nonempty subset of a finite transitive configuration and every nonempty set of at most five points on a circle is Ramsey.
rows.explanation: States the corollary that every set of at most five points on a circle is Ramsey, from the paper's section of geometric consequences and examples of the classification.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization also gives spherical non-Ramsey examples: the specified twelve-point set on the unit circle has a fifty-color obstruction in every positive dimension, and a nine-point circle configuration built from algebraically independent parameters is non-Ramsey.
rows.explanation: States the nine-point non-Ramsey circle configuration built from algebraically independent parameters, a proposition in the paper's section of geometric consequences and examples.

rows.scope_quote: A further sufficient condition uses linear independence of the quadratic evaluation rows of a spherical configuration.
rows.explanation: States the quadratic-independence sufficient condition for spherical configurations to be Ramsey, a proposition in the paper's section of geometric consequences and examples.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization gives the tensor-field classification for full-affine-span configurations, covers singleton and affine-span reductions, and proves that every Ramsey configuration is cospherical.
rows.explanation: States the corollary that every finite Ramsey configuration is spherical, from the paper's section of geometric consequences and examples of the classification.

rows.scope_quote: It also proves that every nonempty subset of a finite transitive configuration and every nonempty set of at most five points on a circle is Ramsey.
rows.explanation: States the corollary that every nonempty subset of a finite transitive configuration is Ramsey, from the paper's section of geometric consequences and examples.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization also gives spherical non-Ramsey examples: the specified twelve-point set on the unit circle has a fifty-color obstruction in every positive dimension, and a nine-point circle configuration built from algebraically independent parameters is non-Ramsey.
rows.explanation: States the twelve-point spherical non-Ramsey example with a fifty-colour obstruction in every dimension, a proposition in the paper's section of geometric consequences and examples of the classification.

rows.scope_quote: Seymour's second-neighborhood conjecture asserts that every nonempty finite oriented graph has a vertex with at least as many second out-neighbors as first out-neighbors. The formalized result proves this assertion, where the second neighborhood consists of vertices at directed distance exactly two. The initial vertex and first neighbors are excluded from that count, and sinks are included.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: every nonempty finite oriented graph has a vertex with at least as many second out-neighbours as first out-neighbours.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization gives one deterministic polynomial-time algorithm and an absolute constant $C>0$ such that a finite $k$-edge-connected loopless multigraph yields a spanning tree using at most a $C/k$ fraction of the edges of every cut. The input may encode parallel-edge multiplicities in binary, and the running time is polynomial in that binary input length.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the algorithmic paper (stated in an input file the dataset's statement list misses): a deterministic polynomial-time construction of C/k-thin spanning trees, with multiplicities in binary.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result gives one absolute constant $C>0$ such that every finite loopless $k$-edge-connected multigraph with at least two vertices has a spanning tree crossing each nontrivial cut at most $(C/k)$ times the original cut size. Parallel edges remain distinct. No numerical value of $C$ or construction algorithm is asserted.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: one constant C such that every k-edge-connected loopless multigraph has a spanning tree using at most a C/k fraction of every cut.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result proves Talagrand's discrete-convexity assertion with $k=2^{75}$. If a family of subsets of a finite nonempty ground set has Bernoulli-$p$ measure at least $1-1/k$, then the sets not contained in a union of $k$ members form a $p$-small family: they have a containment cover of total $p$-cost at most $1/2$. This holds for every $0<p<1$, with repeated members allowed in the union and no monotonicity assumption.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the convexity paper with k = 2^75: a family of Bernoulli-p measure at least 1 − 1/k leaves a p-small family of sets not covered by a union of k members. The two-union corollary is not part of the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result proves $q_f(\mathcal F)\le25\cdot512^4 q(\mathcal F)$ for every nonempty proper increasing family on a finite nonempty ground set. Both thresholds use cover budget $1/2$, and fractional covers may assign weights to every subset, including the empty set.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem with its constant: q_f(F) ≤ 25·512⁴·q(F) for every nonempty proper increasing family.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result proves the comparison up to a universal factor times $1+\log_2|E(H)|$, and hence up to a universal factor times $\log_2 n$, for every graph $H$ with at least one edge and at most $n$ vertices, $n\ge2$. The bounds use the actual containment and expectation thresholds.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem with its explicit constants: p_c(n, H) ≤ min{1, 2048e^50 p_E(n, H)(1 + log₂ e(H))} and the log₂ n form.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization constructs bounded-degree $\mathbb F_2$ coboundary expanders in every dimension $d\ge3$. For each such $d$, it gives finite pure connected $d$-dimensional simplicial complexes with vertex counts tending to infinity, one uniform bound on top-dimensional degree at each vertex, and one positive coboundary-expansion constant in every degree below $d$. The constants may depend on $d$. The graph and two-dimensional cases used for the paper's all-positive-dimensions conclusion are separate.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: bounded-degree F₂ coboundary expanders in every dimension d ≥ 3. The graph and two-dimensional cases behind the all-dimensions statement are separate.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves the circulant Hadamard conjecture in exact form: a real circulant Hadamard matrix of positive order $n$ exists exactly when $n=1$ or $n=4$. Explicit witnesses are supplied for both orders, with no restriction on prime factors.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: a real circulant Hadamard matrix of positive order n exists exactly when n = 1 or n = 4.

rows.scope_quote: It also proves the even-length part of the Barker-sequence consequence. A positive even-length sign sequence whose nonzero aperiodic autocorrelations have absolute value at most one must have length $2$ or $4$. The paper's classification of odd Barker lengths is outside this selected additional statement.
rows.explanation: States the even-length part of the paper's Barker-sequence corollary: even Barker sequences have length 2 or 4. The classification of odd lengths is outside the statement.

rows.scope_quote: Barnette's conjecture states that every finite simple cubic bipartite planar graph that is 3-vertex-connected has a Hamiltonian cycle. The formalization proves this statement for every such graph. The selected result is the existence of a cycle visiting every vertex exactly once.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: every cubic bipartite planar 3-connected graph has a Hamiltonian cycle.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result gives one absolute constant $C>0$ such that every finite simple graph on $n$ vertices has an edge-disjoint decomposition into at most $Cn$ cycles or singleton edges. Edgeless and small graphs are included. The optimal value of $C$ is not determined.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: every graph on n vertices decomposes into at most Cn cycles and single edges. The Eulerian corollary is not part of the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves a fixed power saving for sets with no nonzero square difference. There are absolute constants $c>0$ and $C$ such that every $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ satisfying $a-b\ne m^2$ for all $a,b\in A$ and integers $m\ge1$ has $|A|\le C N^{1-c}$. The bound is uniform for every integer $N\ge1$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: square-difference-free subsets of {1, …, N} have at most CN^{1−c} elements. The polynomial and prime-argument generalisations of the family's later papers are not part of it.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves that some absolute $\varepsilon>0$ and $C$ bound the number of halving pairs by $Cn^{4/3-\varepsilon}$ for every sufficiently large even $n$ and every $n$-point set with no three collinear. It also proves a bound of the same form for all level-switch counts under the additional generic-position assumptions in the statement. The constants are existential.
rows.explanation: States the paper's halving-pair bound Cn^{4/3−ε} and the bound of the same form for level-switch counts under generic position. The k-set corollary is not separately stated.

rows.scope_quote: For every fixed integer $r\ge4$, there is $c_r>0$ such that every finite $K_r$-free simple graph on $n$ vertices with average degree $d\ge2$ has an independent set of size at least $c_r n\log d/d$. The constant depends only on $r$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: for each r ≥ 4, every K_r-free graph with average degree d ≥ 2 has an independent set of size at least c_r n log d/d. The correspondence-colouring result of the family's later paper is not part of the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization constructs two self-dual partitional matroids on one countably infinite ground set that admit neither an independent covering nor a packing/covering partition. The same pair has no intersection witness, so it also refutes the unrestricted infinite matroid intersection conjecture.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: two self-dual partitional matroids on a countable set with neither an independent covering nor a packing/covering partition.

rows.scope_quote: Separate formalized consequences give counterexamples to the individual covering and packing conjectures. The construction is in ordinary set theory with Choice and assumes no finitary restriction on the matroids.
rows.explanation: States the paper's corollaries: the same pair refutes the infinite matroid intersection conjecture, and separate counterexamples refute the covering and packing conjectures.

rows.scope_quote: For every $n\ge2$, every such property invariant under vertex relabeling, and $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, the formalization proves that the edge-probability interval between probabilities $\varepsilon$ and $1-\varepsilon$ has width at most $2^{19}\log(1/(2\varepsilon))/(\log n)^2$. The constant is uniform over the graph property, $n$, and $\varepsilon$.
rows.explanation: States the paper's Friedgut–Kalai theorem with its constant: threshold width at most 2^19 log(1/(2ε))/(log n)² for symmetric increasing graph properties. The variance–influence theorem is not part of the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The linked supplements reconstruct the older $35$-move appendix's finite recursive certificate and prove four conditional winning templates from partial positions, assuming the required Maker cells are present and Breaker avoids the corresponding finite envelope.
rows.explanation: States a reconstruction of the older 35-move appendix certificate, not the 21-move theorem.

rows.scope_quote: The linked supplements reconstruct the older $35$-move appendix's finite recursive certificate and prove four conditional winning templates from partial positions, assuming the required Maker cells are present and Breaker avoids the corresponding finite envelope.
rows.explanation: States conditional winning templates from finite partial positions, supplements to the main strategy rather than the 21-move theorem.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization gives a legal strategy that wins within $21$ actual Maker moves against every legal Breaker play from the empty infinite board. The selected theorem checks disjointness and the move counts throughout play; it does not impose the paper's smaller finite-board restriction.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: one legal Maker policy completing a copy of Snaky within 21 Maker moves against every legal Breaker continuation on the infinite board. The note says the paper's additional finite-board restriction is not imposed.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves that the number of edges at termination, divided by $n^{3/2}$, converges in $L^2$ to $1/(2\sqrt2)$. It also states convergence in probability and convergence of the normalized expectation to the same constant. This is the triangle case of the sharp terminal-leave conjecture of Joos and Kühn.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: the terminal edge count of random triangle removal, divided by n^{3/2}, converges in L² to 1/(2√2).

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves $R(C_m,K_n)=(m-1)(n-1)+1$ for all integers $m\ge n\ge3$ except $(m,n)=(3,3)$, where it proves $R(C_3,K_3)=6$. This is the complete parameter range of the paper's main theorem.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem over its full range: R(C_m, K_n) = (m − 1)(n − 1) + 1 for m ≥ n ≥ 3 except (3, 3), where it is 6.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result disproves a polynomial removal bound for one explicit $66\times66$ binary pattern. For every $c,C>0$, there is an $n\times n$ binary matrix at normalized edit distance at least $\varepsilon>0$ from being pattern-free but with fewer than $c\varepsilon^C n^{132}$ induced ordered copies.
rows.explanation: States the qualitative conclusion of the main theorem for the explicit 66 × 66 pattern: no constants c, C give a polynomial removal bound. The theorem's explicit sizes n_h, distances ε_h and copy bound ε_h 2^{-h} are not asserted.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization constructs an unbounded sequence of sizes $n$ and point sets for which every triangle has area at least $n^{-2+\eta}$, for one fixed $\eta>0$. It consequently refutes the proposed upper bound of order $n^{-2+\varepsilon}$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. The linked construction is for an unbounded sequence of sizes; the paper's statement for every sufficiently large $n$ is broader.
rows.explanation: States the area lower bound n^{-2+η} along an unbounded sequence of sizes, whereas the main theorem gives it for every sufficiently large n; the refutation of the n^{-2+ε} upper bound follows.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization disproves the Gopalan–Servedio square-root degree conjecture by an unbounded factor. For every $C>0$, it gives a nonconstant Boolean function on a finite sign cube for which the sum of its linear Fourier coefficients exceeds $C\sqrt{\deg f}$, where $\deg f$ is its real multilinear degree.
rows.explanation: States both clauses of the main theorem: for every C > 0 a Boolean function whose linear Fourier coefficients sum to more than C√(deg f), and unboundedness of the corresponding ratio.

rows.scope_quote: This selected statement is the complete-domain Dutta comparison. The paper's full flat-local result in arbitrary characteristic is outside it.
rows.explanation: States a supporting characteristic-p comparison over complete local domains (Frobenius multiplicities converge to the Dutta multiplicity, which bounds the Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity). Lech's inequality for flat local maps in arbitrary characteristic is outside it.

rows.scope_quote: The linked formalization verifies only the ring-theoretic candidate: there exists a three-dimensional complete Noetherian integrally closed local domain over $\mathbb C$ whose residue field is $\mathbb C$.
rows.explanation: States only that the candidate ring is a three-dimensional complete Noetherian normal local domain over C with residue field C, one of the five supporting comparisons named in the Comparator README. The absence of a small Cohen–Macaulay module, the paper's claim, is outside this statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result constructs a finitely presented torsion-free group $G$ and nonzero elements $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb F_2[G]$ with $\alpha\beta=0$, giving a counterexample.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem including its second clause: a finitely presented torsion-free group with zero divisors in F₂[G] that admits a finite two-dimensional classifying space.

rows.scope_quote: It gives a finitely generated group $G$ and an $n\times n$ matrix over $\mathbb Z[G]$, with $n\ge1$, that is invertible over $\mathbb Q[G]$. Its bounded left-regular operator is invertible and has determinant strictly between $0$ and $1$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: a matrix over Z[G] invertible over Q[G] with Fuglede–Kadison determinant strictly between 0 and 1. The theorem's statement that the spectral integral is negative is not included, though the note records that for invertible matrices it is equivalent to the determinant bound.

rows.scope_quote: One statement records the counterexample for a finitely generated group; the more detailed construction gives a finitely presented group with an element of odd prime order.
rows.explanation: States a characteristic-two counterexample to direct finiteness over a finitely generated group, without the finite presentation and odd-order torsion of the main theorem; KaplanskyFinitelyPresented records those.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized results construct a finite field of characteristic two and a group algebra violating this implication. One statement records the counterexample for a finitely generated group; the more detailed construction gives a finitely presented group with an element of odd prime order.
rows.explanation: States the existence assertion of the main theorem: a finite field of characteristic two, a finitely presented group with an element of odd prime order, and a, b with ab = 1, ba ≠ 1. The theorem's description of the data by a terminating prescription is not part of the statement.

rows.scope_quote: Let $p$ be the smallest prime divisor of $\bigl(\binom{1200}{600}!\bigr)^2+1$; this prime is odd. The formalized result constructs a field $K$ of order $p^4$, a finitely generated group $G$ with torsion, and elements $a,b$ violating this implication.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the odd-characteristic paper: with p the least prime factor of (C(1200, 600)!)² + 1, a field of order p⁴, a finitely generated group with torsion and a, b with ab = 1, ba ≠ 1.

rows.scope_quote: A separate formalized result gives a finite-dimensional complex algebra whose little and big finitistic dimensions are infinite on the left and zero on the right. Injectives fail to generate its unbounded derived category on the left and generate it on the right.
rows.explanation: States the paper's corollary: an algebra whose finitistic dimensions are infinite on the left and zero on the right, with the corresponding behaviour of injective generation.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized counterexample is a finite-dimensional complex algebra with a finitely generated module of projective dimension at least $2m-2$ and still finite for every $m\ge1$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: a finite-dimensional complex algebra with finitely generated modules of finite projective dimension at least 2m − 2 for every m.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized counterexample is a finite-dimensional algebra over $k=\mathbb F_2(q,H_1,H_2)$ and a finite-dimensional nonprojective Gorenstein-projective module with this vanishing.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: over k = F₂(q, H₁, H₂), a finite-dimensional algebra and a nonprojective Gorenstein-projective module with the Auslander–Reiten vanishing, with the stated structural properties.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized counterexample gives a finite-dimensional symmetric algebra over $\mathbb F_2(q,H_1,H_2)$ and a finite-dimensional nonprojective module $M$ with $\mathrm{Ext}^i(M,M)=0$ for every $i>0$. Symmetric algebras are self-injective, so this contradicts the conjecture.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: a symmetric algebra over F₂(q, H₁, H₂) with a nonprojective module whose positive self-Ext groups vanish. The field-extension and homological corollaries are not included.

rows.scope_quote: Saxl's conjecture asserts that the tensor square of each staircase Specht module contains every irreducible representation of the corresponding symmetric group. The formalization establishes this for every $m\ge1$: if $\rho_m=(m,m-1,\ldots,1)$, then $g(\rho_m,\rho_m,\mu)>0$ for every partition $\mu$ of $m(m+1)/2$.
rows.explanation: States Saxl's conjecture as stated in the cyclic-polytabloid paper: the tensor square of every staircase Specht module contains every irreducible representation. The stronger orbit-span claim is not included.

rows.scope_quote: For every positive integer $n\notin\{2,4,9\}$, it constructs an irreducible complex representation of $S_n$ whose tensor square contains every irreducible complex representation of $S_n$. Equivalently, all corresponding Kronecker coefficients are positive. The statement also supplies injective intertwining maps for arbitrary finite-dimensional irreducible representations.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: for every n ∉ {2, 4, 9}, an irreducible representation of S_n whose tensor square contains every irreducible representation.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves the paper's colored-graph characterization: a finite nonempty lattice is representable exactly when it admits the specified finite nonempty graph witness, whose edge colors encode the required congruence relations. This selected theorem is the equivalence with the graph criterion; the paper's undecidability and subgroup-interval conclusions are outside it.
rows.explanation: States part (i) of the main theorem, the coloured-graph characterisation of representable finite lattices. The undecidability and subgroup-interval parts are outside the statement.

rows.scope_quote: For torsion-free $G$, it identifies the trace on $K_0(\mathbb C[G])$ with the integral augmentation rank and proves the characteristic-zero Kaplansky idempotent conjecture: for every commutative unital domain $R$ of characteristic zero, an idempotent in $R[G]$ is $0$ or $1$.
rows.explanation: States the paper's torsion-free corollary: the trace on K₀ equals the augmentation rank, and Kaplansky's idempotent conjecture holds in characteristic zero.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves the complex Bass trace conjecture for every group: the Hattori–Stallings trace of each virtual class of finitely generated projective right $\mathbb C[G]$-modules vanishes on conjugacy classes of infinite-order elements. No finiteness, countability, or geometric hypothesis on $G$ is imposed.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: for every group G the Hattori–Stallings trace of projective C[G]-modules vanishes on conjugacy classes of infinite-order elements.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result proves surjectivity of the canonical averaged Foulkes–Howe map $\mathrm{Sym}^b(\mathrm{Sym}^a\,V)\to\mathrm{Sym}^a(\mathrm{Sym}^b\,V)$ for every finite-dimensional complex vector space, $a\ge2$, and $b\ge a(a-1)$. It also covers the bijective $a=1$ case, the vanishing-on-products consequence, and the corresponding equivariant embedding in the reverse direction. The sixth-power specialization is covered for $b\ge30$; the companion's full range $b\ge6$ is not included.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: the canonical Foulkes–Howe map is surjective for a ≥ 2 and b ≥ a(a − 1). The companion paper's sixth-power result for the full range b ≥ 6 is not included.

rows.scope_quote: For every fixed $q>4$, the formalization proves the Brownian continuum-random-tree limit for critical finite Fortuin–Kasteleyn planar maps. After rescaling graph distances in an $n$-edge map by a constant depending on $q$ times $n^{-1/2}$ and using normalized degree measure, the metric-measure space converges in distribution to the Brownian continuum random tree in the Gromov–Hausdorff–Prokhorov topology. The convergence holds through all positive integer sizes.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: for q > 4, critical finite Fortuin–Kasteleyn planar maps, with distances rescaled by c(q)n^{-1/2}, converge to the Brownian continuum random tree in the Gromov–Hausdorff–Prokhorov topology.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves differentiability of the planar first-passage time-constant norm for independent Gamma edge weights of every positive shape and rate. The norm is differentiable away from the origin, and its unit sphere has a $C^1$ boundary.
rows.explanation: States the paper's theorem on Gamma weights: the time-constant norm is differentiable away from the origin for every positive shape and rate.

rows.scope_quote: The paper also claims strict convexity for the exponential limit shape. Strict convexity is outside these selected differentiability statements.
rows.explanation: States the differentiability half of the exponential limit-shape theorem, with a unique supporting line at every boundary point. The strict convexity asserted in the same theorem is outside the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves absence of an infinite cluster at criticality for Bernoulli bond percolation on every infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive graph with critical probability $p_c<1$. At $p=p_c$, the probability that any infinite cluster exists is zero. The graph model permits bond multiplicities.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the quasi-transitive paper: no infinite cluster at p_c for bond percolation on every infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive graph with p_c < 1.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result proves that, at their respective critical probabilities, nearest-neighbor bond and site percolation on $\mathbb Z^3$ almost surely have no infinite cluster. Equivalently, almost surely every vertex belongs to a finite cluster in each model.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: no infinite cluster at criticality for nearest-neighbour bond and site percolation on Z³.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves the nonuniqueness phase conjecture for Bernoulli bond percolation on infinite connected locally finite nonamenable quasi-transitive graphs. It establishes $p_c<p_{2\to2}\le p_u$ and a common nonempty coupled interval with infinitely many infinite clusters almost surely.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem (p_c < p_{2→2} ≤ p_u with infinitely many infinite clusters on a common interval) together with the Cayley-graph and critical-law corollaries.

rows.scope_quote: For Cayley graphs, the result holds for every finite symmetric generating set of a nonamenable finitely generated group and every $p\in(p_c,p_u)$.
rows.explanation: States the paper's corollary for Cayley graphs: nonuniqueness for every finite symmetric generating set of a nonamenable group and every p in (p_c, p_u).

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result proves exponential decay of spin correlations for the two-dimensional classical $O(n)$ model at every temperature when $n\ge3$. For each interaction bound $\beta>0$, constants $A$ and $m>0$ work for every finite square-lattice subgraph with free boundary and nonnegative edge strengths at most $\beta$: the correlation between sites $x,y$ is at most $Ae^{-m|x-y|}$. The infinite-volume limit and the separate $O(4)$ spectral-gap claim are not included.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: exponential decay of spin correlations in the two-dimensional O(n) model, n ≥ 3, at every temperature, uniformly over finite subgraphs with free boundary. The infinite-volume corollary is not included.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result compares conditional Ising probabilities on finite graphs when two boundary mixtures differ but a common set of spins is pinned. If $q_0$ is the associated zero-field Fortuin–Kasteleyn connection probability after deleting the pinned vertices, the likelihood ratio lies between $\exp(-4\mathrm{artanh}\,q_0)$ and $\exp(4\mathrm{artanh}\,q_0)$. The statement allows arbitrary external fields and arbitrary probability mixtures satisfying the stated disjointness conditions. The paper's finite stopping-band approximation theorem is outside this selected statement.
rows.explanation: States the paper's finite-graph comparison theorem: conditional Ising likelihood ratios lie between exp(∓4 artanh q₀). The stopping-band resolution theorem is outside the statement.

rows.scope_quote: For an i.i.d. uniformly elliptic nearest-neighbor random environment on $\mathbb Z^d$, the formalization proves that almost-sure directional transience implies convergence of $X_n/n$ to a deterministic velocity with positive projection in that direction for every $d\ge2$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: in uniformly elliptic i.i.d. environments, almost-sure directional transience implies ballisticity with a deterministic velocity, for d ≥ 2.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves this for nearest-neighbor walks in independent identically distributed strictly elliptic environments on $\mathbb Z^d$, for every $d\ge3$ and every nonzero real direction. Strict ellipticity means that every allowed transition probability is positive almost surely; no uniform positive lower bound or moment condition is assumed. The probability is the annealed law from the origin.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: the directional zero–one law for random walks in i.i.d. strictly elliptic environments on Z^d, d ≥ 3.

rows.scope_quote: For $d\ge3$, positive probability of transience in any nonzero direction already suffices. The limiting velocity is unique, and the unit directions with positive transience probability are exactly the open hemisphere having positive inner product with that velocity; transience has probability one on that hemisphere and zero on its complement. The environment is sampled once and retained along the walk, and the probabilities use the annealed law from the origin.
rows.explanation: States the paper's corollary for d ≥ 3: positive probability of transience suffices, and the transient directions form the open hemisphere determined by the velocity.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves the Mézard–Parisi hierarchical cavity formula for diluted even-arity Ising models in the Panchenko–Talagrand class. Under the class's factorization, independence, integrability, and positivity assumptions, the finite-system pressure converges to the infimum of the trial functional over all finite hierarchy depths and trial laws. The arity is any even integer at least two and the interaction density is positive.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: the Mézard–Parisi formula, with existence of the thermodynamic limit, for diluted even-arity models in the Panchenko–Talagrand class.

rows.scope_quote: This is a supporting well-definedness result. It does not assert convergence of the finite-system pressure or the paper's extension to all bounded Borel log-potentials.
rows.explanation: States that the variational value for the Ising perceptron is a finite real number, a well-definedness result. Convergence of the pressure, the paper's main theorem, is not asserted.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves the variational formula for the spherical random perceptron's limiting pressure for every positive pattern density and inverse temperature and every bounded continuous single-pattern potential. It shows that the variational value is finite and that the pressure converges to it both in expectation and in probability.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the spherical paper: the limiting pressure of the spherical perceptron equals the variational formula for every positive density and inverse temperature and every bounded continuous potential.

rows.scope_quote: The linked spherical-field result supplies a supporting dual formula: finite hierarchy field values converge uniformly on compact parameter sets to an attained dual minimum, and the corresponding bounded stationary-field approximation holds for monotone overlap quantiles bounded away from one.
rows.explanation: States a supporting dual formula for spherical linear fields and a bounded stationary-field approximation, not the pressure formula itself.

rows.scope_quote: For deterministic times $t_n=o(n^{2/3})$ or update counts $k_n=o(n^{5/3})$, the Gibbs mass of realized starting states still farther than $1/4$ from equilibrium tends to one in probability. For every deterministic positive sequence $M_n\to\infty$, the covariance operator norm and the linear Rayleigh supremum, using the unscaled heat-bath Dirichlet form, both lie between $n^{2/3}/M_n$ and $M_n n^{2/3}$ with probability tending to one. The covariance result does not give an upper bound for the full inverse spectral gap.
rows.explanation: States the critical paper's theorems on realised equilibrium starts and on covariance and linear tests at scale n^{2/3}, with the mixing lower bounds. The covariance result gives no upper bound for the inverse spectral gap.

rows.scope_quote: At criticality in the zero-field Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model, the formalization proves that for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, the continuous-time mixing time lies between $n^{2/3-\varepsilon}$ and $e^{\varepsilon n}$, and the discrete-time mixing count lies between $n^{5/3-\varepsilon}$ and $e^{\varepsilon n}$, with probability tending to one over the Gaussian disorder. The disorder has independent off-diagonal entries of variance $1/n$. Continuous updates have rate one per site; discrete time counts uniformly chosen single-site update attempts. Mixing is worst-start total variation at threshold $1/4$, with holding allowed.
rows.explanation: States the critical-slowing-down paper's mixing bounds at β = 1: continuous-time mixing between n^{2/3−ε} and e^{εn}, and discrete counts between n^{5/3−ε} and e^{εn}, with probability tending to one.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves a stretched-exponential mixing obstruction for the zero-field Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model at every fixed inverse temperature $\beta>1$. At time $\exp(n^{1/10000})$, the expected Gibbs mass of initial configurations whose total-variation distance from equilibrium exceeds $1/4$ tends to one. Since this mass lies in $[0,1]$, it also tends to one in probability over the disorder.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the barriers paper: for β > 1, at time exp(n^{1/10000}) most equilibrium starting states are still farther than 1/4 from equilibrium.

rows.scope_quote: For every fixed inverse temperature $0<\beta<1$, the formalization proves a dimension-independent Poincaré inequality for the zero-field Gaussian Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model with probability tending to one over the disorder. Equivalently, the unscaled single-site heat-bath spectral gap stays bounded away from zero. For dynamics that choose one site uniformly at each discrete step, the spectral gap is at least $1/(Cn)$ with probability tending to one, for a constant $C$ depending on $\beta$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: for 0 < β < 1, a dimension-free Poincaré inequality for the SK Gibbs measure with probability tending to one, equivalently a spectral gap bounded away from zero.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized supporting result proves ratio cutoff for discrete single-site heat-bath dynamics in the zero-field Gaussian Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model for $0\le\beta<1/2$. For every $0<\varepsilon<1/2$ and $\eta>0$, the probability over the disorder that $t_{\mathrm{mix}}(\varepsilon)/t_{\mathrm{mix}}(1-\varepsilon)>1+\eta$ tends to zero as $n\to\infty$.
rows.explanation: States ratio cutoff, t_mix(ε)/t_mix(1 − ε) → 1 in probability, for discrete dynamics and β < 1/2 only, which the note calls supporting. The cutoff theorem of the paper covers every β < 1 with an explicit cutoff location and continuous time.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization constructs one stable radial pair potential in three-dimensional continuum space with a divergent repulsive core and an integrable tail that is $o(r^{-3})$. Its canonical free energy exists for every positive inverse temperature and density. At one inverse temperature $\beta_c\in(1/2,3/2)$, the free energy has a strict finite jump between its one-sided derivatives with respect to inverse temperature, for every density in one nonempty open interval.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: a stable radial potential in R³ with divergent core and o(r^{-3}) tail whose free energy has a derivative jump at one β_c for every density in an open interval.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization constructs a bounded continuous stable radial pair potential in $\mathbb R^3$ satisfying $|\phi(r)|\le Cr^{-3-1/32}$ for $r\ge1$. There is a nonempty open interval of positive densities around $5p/3$, where $p$ is the unit-separated packing-density limit, on which the canonical free energy exists at every positive inverse temperature and has a strict downward derivative jump at one common $\beta_c\in[7/8,9/8]$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the algebraic-decay paper: a bounded continuous stable potential with |φ(r)| ≤ Cr^{-3-1/32} and a common derivative jump at β_c in [7/8, 9/8] for every density in an open interval around 5p/3.

rows.scope_quote: The earlier fixed-density statement at $5p/3$ is also retained. Both statements concern the derivative with respect to inverse temperature.
rows.explanation: States the earlier fixed-density statement at the single density 5p/3, whereas the main theorem gives a common transition temperature for every density in an open interval; the interval version is RadialDensityInterval.

rows.scope_quote: The selected statements cover reconstruction above the Kesten–Stigum threshold. Non-reconstruction at or below the threshold and the stochastic-block-model consequences in the paper are outside them.
rows.explanation: States the reconstruction direction of the exact-threshold theorem (reconstruction when dλ² > 1 on regular and Poisson trees). Non-reconstruction at or below the threshold, the other direction, is outside the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The selected statements cover reconstruction above the Kesten–Stigum threshold. Non-reconstruction at or below the threshold and the stochastic-block-model consequences in the paper are outside them.
rows.explanation: States the same reconstruction direction above the Kesten–Stigum threshold as ThreeStateSupercritical, in a separately written statement; non-reconstruction is outside it.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves that every continuous nondecreasing Hausdorff gauge agreeing with $h(r)=r^d(\log\log(1/r))^{(2-d)/2}$ at sufficiently small positive radii almost surely assigns positive measure to every nontrivial compact positive-time segment of ordinary chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa$.
rows.explanation: States the positivity half of the explicit-gauge theorem: the gauge r^d(log log(1/r))^{(2−d)/2} gives positive measure to every positive-time segment of chordal SLE_κ. Finiteness of that measure and the expectation bound are not included.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves that the free uniform spanning forest is a factor of independent identically distributed vertex labels on every infinite connected locally finite simple unweighted graph. One Borel equivariant rule works for all such graphs and uses no distinguished root.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: one Borel root-independent equivariant rule makes the free uniform spanning forest a factor of IID on every infinite connected locally finite graph.

rows.scope_quote: The linked supplements also give equivariant IID sampling for invariant strongly Rayleigh laws on countable groups and existence, uniqueness, and IID-factor results for determinantal laws with Hermitian positive-contraction kernels on countable index sets. These group results require neither amenability nor finite generation, and the kernels need not be trace class.
rows.explanation: States IID factors for invariant strongly Rayleigh laws on countable groups and the determinantal results, which the paper states as a theorem and corollary in its introduction and the note calls supplements to the spanning-forest theorem (FreeUniformSpanningForest).

rows.scope_quote: The formalization gives variational limits for orthogonally invariant Ising spin glasses whose eigenvectors have Haar law and whose empirical eigenvalue distributions converge to a compactly supported law with the stated control of extreme eigenvalues. The pressure converges both in expectation and almost surely to an explicit functional of the limiting spectral law. A version with external fields assumes convergence of their empirical laws in Wasserstein distance and gives the corresponding magnetic-field functional.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem (limiting pressure of orthogonally invariant Ising spin glasses, in expectation and almost surely) with the field, ground-state, random-spectrum and Gaussian-pattern versions.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves that every fixed integer $k\ge3$ has a finite positive threshold $\alpha_k$: for every fixed density $c<\alpha_k$, the satisfiability probability tends to one as the number of variables grows, while for every $c>\alpha_k$ it tends to zero. Clauses use distinct variables with independent uniform signs and are sampled independently with replacement. The statement makes no assertion at the threshold itself.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: for every k ≥ 3 a limiting satisfiability threshold α_k exists, with no assertion at the threshold itself.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves that the limiting threshold $\alpha$ for uniform random $3$-SAT is a computable positive real. Satisfiability tends to one at every fixed density below $\alpha$ and to zero at every fixed density above it. One deterministic machine produces a rational number $q_r$ for every requested precision $r$ with $|q_r-\alpha|\le2^{-r}$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: the random 3-SAT threshold exists and is a computable real, approximable to precision 2^{-r} by one machine.

rows.scope_quote: The linked supplements prove sharpness of the separate survival-lifetime and clause-replacement estimates used in the argument. They do not show that the logarithmic factor in the $k=3$ variance bound is necessary.
rows.explanation: States sharpness of auxiliary survival-lifetime and clause-replacement estimates used in the variance argument.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves $\mathrm{Var}(H_n)=\Theta_k(n)$ for every fixed $k\ge4$. For $k=3$, it proves a positive linear lower bound and an $O(n\log n)$ upper bound. The same upper bounds hold after clipping at any fixed positive multiple of $n$, and linear lower bounds hold for sufficiently high clipping levels.
rows.explanation: States the variance theorem for the unsatisfiability hitting time: Θ_k(n) for k ≥ 4, and between linear and O(n log n) for k = 3. The linear k = 3 bound of the family's later paper is not part of it.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result determines the factor-of-IID threshold for the free zero-field Ising law on the infinite $d$-regular tree. For every $d\ge3$ and $\beta\ge0$, the law is a factor of IID exactly when $\tanh\beta\le1/\sqrt{d-1}$, including equality. The factor uses independent uniform vertex labels and is almost surely equivariant for each fixed tree automorphism. Finitary coding and coding-radius bounds are not included.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: the free Ising law on the d-regular tree is a factor of IID exactly when tanh β ≤ 1/√(d − 1). Finitary coding bounds are not included.

rows.scope_quote: For critical self-avoiding walks on the honeycomb lattice, the formalization proves that the total weight of paths crossing a strip of height $N$ is comparable to $N^{-1/4}$, while the first horizontal-displacement moment of return paths is comparable to $N^{3/4}$. It also proves finiteness of the strip sums, the exact arch–bridge balance identity, comparison of successive moment increments with bridge mass, and monotonicity of bridge mass. The comparison constants are uniform in the strip height.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the strip-mass paper: strip-crossing weight comparable to N^{-1/4} and return-path displacement moment comparable to N^{3/4}, with uniform constants, finiteness and the balance identity.

rows.scope_quote: These are supporting summability statements. The paper's $h^{4/3+o(1)}$ mean-length law and its central-visit and hexagonal-chord exponents are outside them.
rows.explanation: States finiteness of critical bridge weights and first length moments, which the note calls supporting summability statements. The h^{4/3+o(1)} mean-length law and the other exponents of the paper are outside them.

rows.scope_quote: This includes finiteness of the path sum. The prescribed-endpoint length law, arch and strip mean laws, and remaining moment and renewal conclusions are outside this supporting statement.
rows.explanation: States the two-sided bound B_h ≍ (1 + h)^{-1/4} on strict bridge mass, an input estimate for the prescribed-endpoint paper and one of the five supporting comparisons named in the Comparator README. The theorem's docstring in the challenge file reads "Trusted reference hole only; missing necessary main obligation."

rows.scope_quote: This selected result supplies the limiting free energy. It does not state the paper's small-force exponent, near-critical correlation scale, or the $3/4$ spatial and moment laws.
rows.explanation: States existence of the infinite-length free energy for the critical honeycomb walk with a force parameter. The small-force exponent, correlation scale and the 3/4 spatial and moment laws are not stated.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized binary-sweep theorem gives a universal power contraction in every irreducible representation: for sufficiently large $d$, the averaged sweep on $2^d$ slots has operator norm at most $D^{-g}$ in representation dimension $D$, for some $g>0$. The sign expectation is zero, and a fixed number of independent sweeps approaches uniform in total variation from every initial deck.
rows.explanation: States the binary sweep theorem: operator norm at most D^{-g} in every irreducible representation, with mixing after a fixed number of sweeps. Identification with the physical shuffle law is not included.

rows.scope_quote: A separate conditional moment estimate covers allowed power-of-two grids and disjoint coordinate-respecting trajectories, with its stated feasibility premise. Physical-shuffle law identification is not included.
rows.explanation: States the conditional moment estimate for grids and prescribed trajectories under its feasibility premise, a theorem in Section 3 of the paper rather than its headline sweep theorem.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves a uniform trace-smoothing estimate for coordinate sweeps of the Thorp shuffle on $2^d$ cards. One absolute sweep parameter works for every $d\ge1$: the regular trace is at most $1+(2^d)^{-10}$, and the full permutation law after the corresponding fixed number of sweeps is within $\tfrac12(2^d)^{-5}$ of uniform in total variation, for every initial deck. Thus the selected upper bound uses $O(d)$ physical shuffles.
rows.explanation: States the trace-smoothing theorem: regular trace at most 1 + (2^d)^{-10}, and the permutation law after a fixed number of sweeps within ½(2^d)^{-5} of uniform.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves the paper's strict four-row permanent inequality. There are constants $4/3<p<2$ and $\varepsilon>0$ such that every probability law on $S_4$ within total-variation distance $\varepsilon$ of uniform, and with exactly uniform coordinate marginals, satisfies the permanent bound by the product of the four $L^p$ row norms for every nonnegative matrix. The exponent and neighborhood are uniform over those laws. The Thorp mixing consequence is outside this selected statement.
rows.explanation: States the paper's robust four-row permanent inequality near the uniform law on S₄. The Thorp mixing consequence is outside the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The supporting row–column estimate bounds the total squared overlap over all multiplicity copies on an occupied board, with explicit dependence on the row and column representation dimensions, the global dimension, the number of missing cells, and the number of rows or columns containing the global Young diagram. The paper's full physical-mixing conclusion is outside these selected representation estimates.
rows.explanation: States the supporting row–column overlap estimate on occupied boards. Five definitions are Comparator holes; the library body of the endpoint statement OccupiedOverlapEndpoint matches the challenge file.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized supporting result turns bounds on partial-permutation cosets into Fourier bounds. Partition a finite set into $b\ge1$ nonempty blocks, and let $f\ge0$ be a subprobability weight on its symmetric group whose left-coset masses for each block subgroup are at most $B$. For every irreducible unitary representation of dimension $D$ and every $u>0$, both the squared Hilbert–Schmidt norm and squared operator norm of its Fourier transform are at most $bB\,C(u)D^{-1+(u+2)/b}$, where $C(u)$ is the stated symmetric-group degree constant.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the partial-permutation paper: coset-mass bounds for a block partition give Fourier bounds bB·C(u)·D^{-1+(u+2)/b}. The paper's asymptotic conclusion about products of random permutations is outside it.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization gives signed representation estimates for coordinate sweeps of the Thorp shuffle. For every signed occurrence of a Young diagram of size $2^d$, it bounds the logarithm of a fixed-order weighted sweep moment by a small multiple of the signed partition entropy plus an explicit remainder-size budget. The moment order is uniform over the diagrams and decompositions after the two small coefficients are fixed.
rows.explanation: States the paper's moment bound for every signed occurrence of a Young diagram, uniform over diagrams. The full-deck convergence corollary is not part of the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The linked supporting angle bound controls the overlap of row, column, and global signed-type projections on an occupied rectangle, with explicit entropy, dimension, and missing-cell factors. These selected estimates support the paper's full-density argument; the full $L^2$ and total-variation mixing conclusion is outside them.
rows.explanation: States the supporting angle bound for signed spin types on occupied rectangles. Its three Comparator holes have library bodies matching the challenge file.

rows.scope_quote: The linked supporting results include frame and conditional-list estimates, regular trace and spectral bounds, signed moments, and full-density $L^2$ control. They also bound reciprocal Specht-dimension sums and give the eight-block Fourier estimate used in the mixing argument.
rows.explanation: States supporting estimates for the mixing argument: bounds on reciprocal Specht-dimension sums and the eight-block Fourier estimate.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves optimal-order mixing of the Thorp shuffle on $2^d$ cards. After $1600d$ complete shuffles, the full permutation law converges in total variation to uniform as $d\to\infty$, uniformly over initial decks. Together with the support lower bound of $2d-O(1)$, this gives mixing time $\Theta(d)=\Theta(\log(2^d))$.
rows.explanation: Bundles supporting estimates with full-deck mixing after 32800d steps and mixing time Θ(log 2^d). This states the optimal order of the main theorem with a worse constant: the theorem states mixing after 1600d shuffles.

rows.scope_quote: The conditional high-height estimate requires a sufficiently large cutoff height $J$ that exceeds twice the number $s$ of coordinates in the fixed low block, so $J>2s$. These are the earlier nine statements associated with the paper; its changed later statements and six other result blocks are outside this scope.
rows.explanation: States nine routing and representation estimates that the note calls the earlier statements associated with the paper, with its changed later statements outside. Whether any of the nine is the current main theorem on routing density and representation contraction would need a line-by-line comparison.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result is the weighted compatibility theorem for balanced $A\times D$ rectangles, with $n=AD$ and $\sqrt n/2\le A,D\le2\sqrt n$. For arbitrary nonnegative weights on the row and column permutation groups, the normalized compatibility average is bounded by $\exp(C_0n^{54/100})$ times the product of the marginal $L^{1/\theta}$ factors, where $\theta=1-L/\log\sqrt n>0$ and the constants are absolute. Compatibility means injectivity in every original column. The bounded regular-moment and other moment/rank conclusions are not included.
rows.explanation: States the paper's weighted compatibility theorem for balanced rectangles. The bounded regular-moment theorem and the rank and mixing consequences are not included.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves uniform representation bounds for one coordinate sweep of the Thorp shuffle. For each irreducible representation of dimension $D$, it chooses a weight between $D^{3/4}$ and $D$ and a Schatten exponent bounded by one absolute constant so that the weighted Schatten moment is at most one. The sweep's operator norm is consequently at most $D^{-c}$ for one absolute $c>0$.
rows.explanation: States the paper's weighted sweep-moment theorem: for each irreducible representation, a weighted Schatten moment at most one, hence operator norm at most D^{-c}. The mixing corollary is outside the statement.

rows.scope_quote: Under the continuum hypothesis, the formalized result refutes the proposed transfer of categoricity down to the Hanf threshold. It gives an abstract elementary class in a countable relational language, with Löwenheim–Skolem number $\aleph_0$, that has two nonisomorphic models at $\beth_{\omega_2}=h(\aleph_0)$ but is categorical in every cardinal at least $\beth_{(2^{\aleph_1})^+}$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: under CH, an abstract elementary class with two nonisomorphic models at the Hanf threshold that is categorical in all large cardinals.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result gives a negative answer: every order automorphism of the full Turing degrees of subsets of $\mathbb N$ fixes every degree, with no definability or genericity assumption. The additional representation corollaries are not included.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: every automorphism of the Turing degrees is the identity. The representation corollaries are not included.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization establishes this for every recursively enumerable subset of $\mathbb N^n$, $n\ge1$: an integer polynomial has exactly one complete natural-number witness tuple for members and none for nonmembers.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: every recursively enumerable set has a single-fold Diophantine representation. The undecidability corollary is not separately formalised.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result separates polynomial time from choiceless polynomial time with counting. It gives an explicit query on finite structures with eight relations that is invariant under isomorphism and decidable in polynomial time, but is not definable in the stated hereditarily finite-set language with cardinality and polynomial bounds on stages and intermediate objects. The query applies to all finite inputs without a promise. The separate witnessed-symmetric-choice result is not included.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: an isomorphism-invariant polynomial-time query on eight-relation structures not definable in choiceless polynomial time with counting.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves that witnessed symmetric choice strictly increases the expressive power of choiceless polynomial time with counting. It constructs one fixed sentence with exactly one witnessed-choice occurrence that gives a Boolean answer on every finite input, while no sentence of the original counting formalism defines the same class of inputs.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: one sentence with a single witnessed symmetric choice defines a class that no sentence of choiceless polynomial time with counting defines.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves the relative-consistency implication: if ZF is consistent, then so is ZF with the Partition Principle, Choice for ordinal-indexed families, and failure of the Axiom of Choice.
rows.explanation: States the main consistency theorem: if ZF is consistent, so is ZF with the Partition Principle, ordinal-indexed choice and the failure of the Axiom of Choice.

rows.scope_quote: The linked model-construction result also constructs a transitive model of the Partition Principle without Choice from an externally countable transitive ground model satisfying the stated axioms, including Choice, and containing an internal strongly inaccessible cardinal. The paper's stronger transitive-model preservation assertions are outside that selected construction.
rows.explanation: States a transitive model of the Partition Principle without Choice from a countable transitive ground model that also contains a strongly inaccessible cardinal, an assumption the paper's transitive-model theorem does not make; the theorem's preservation assertions are outside the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves the $\beta$-Barendregt–Geuvers–Klop conjecture for pure type systems: if every legal expression in every valid context has some terminating $\beta$-reduction sequence, then every $\beta$-reduction sequence from every such expression terminates. Reduction is allowed inside type annotations, and the specification may have arbitrary sorts and nonfunctional axioms or rules.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: in every pure type system, weak β-normalisation of all legal expressions implies strong normalisation.

rows.scope_quote: Cannon's conjecture asks whether a hyperbolic group with boundary homeomorphic to the two-sphere acts geometrically on hyperbolic three-space. The formalization proves that such a group admits an isometric action on $\mathbb H^3$ that is proper and cocompact and has finite kernel. Hyperbolicity is expressed through uniformly thin geodesic triangles in a Cayley graph, and the boundary hypothesis is a homeomorphism with $S^2$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem (Cannon's conjecture): a hyperbolic group with two-sphere boundary acts properly and cocompactly by isometries on H³ with finite kernel.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization gives a negative answer by constructing an infinite finitely presented periodic group, including a witness realized as a Steinberg group over an algebra of characteristic two. Periodicity means that each element has some finite order; no common exponent is asserted. The paper's separate nil-algebra and radical-algebra conclusions are outside these selected statements.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: an infinite finitely presented periodic group, realised as St₁₂(R) for an F₂-algebra R. The nil-algebra conclusions and the Kazhdan corollary are not part of the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result rules out such a mean for the standard group of dyadic piecewise-linear homeomorphisms of the interval, proving nonamenability. No explicit boundary constant or prescribed generating set is given.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: Thompson's group F admits no invariant mean, so it is not amenable.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization constructs a finitely generated residually finite group of cohomological dimension two that has a three-dimensional classifying space but no two-dimensional one. Thus its geometric dimension is three, contradicting the conjecture.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: a finitely generated residually finite group of cohomological dimension two and geometric dimension three.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves the equivalence in full: a finitely generated group has a computable word problem for a finite generating set exactly when it embeds by an injective homomorphism into a finitely presented simple group.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: a finitely generated group has decidable word problem exactly when it embeds in a finitely presented simple group.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves the higher-finiteness strengthening of the Boone–Higman conjecture: every finitely generated group with decidable word problem embeds by an injective homomorphism into a nontrivial simple group of type $F_\infty$. Here type $F_\infty$ means that the group has a classifying CW complex with finitely many cells in each dimension. No additional finiteness property of the original group is assumed.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the higher-finiteness paper: every finitely generated group with decidable word problem embeds in a nontrivial simple group of type F_∞.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result constructs one group $H$ of type $F_\infty$ containing every finitely presented group. Here type $F_\infty$ means that $H$ has a classifying space with finitely many cells in each dimension.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: one group of type F_∞ containing every finitely presented group. The corollary characterising its finitely generated subgroups is not included.
