rows.scope_quote: The Hilbert space can be chosen separable for countable groups; a separate linked statement records a separable witness with uniform bound $101$ in that case.
rows.explanation: States that every countable nonamenable group has a nonunitarisable representation on a separable Hilbert space with uniform bound 101; the main theorem gives the bound 1 + ε, the converse direction and all discrete groups.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization establishes this equivalence for every discrete group.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: a discrete group is amenable exactly when it is unitarisable, with nonunitarisable representations of bound at most 1 + ε for every nonamenable group.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result gives a negative answer by constructing a torsion-free word-hyperbolic group that is not residually finite.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: a torsion-free word-hyperbolic group that is not residually finite. The nonlinearity corollary is not a separate conclusion of the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result answers the existence question affirmatively: there is one group that is infinite, finitely presented, simple, and amenable. Amenability is expressed by the Følner condition.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: an infinite finitely presented simple amenable group, with amenability in Følner form.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result gives a counterexample: an Artin group defined by a symmetric matrix on $116$ generators, with diagonal entries $1$ and off-diagonal entries in $\{2,3,\infty\}$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: an Artin group on 116 generators with labels in {2, 3, ∞} that acts geometrically on no proper CAT(0) space.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves that the intersection of any family of parabolic subgroups of a finite-rank Artin group is parabolic. Every such intersection is already the intersection of at most the rank many members, and every subset has a unique parabolic closure. Both finite and infinite Coxeter labels are allowed.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem (intersections of parabolic subgroups are parabolic) with the corollaries on arbitrary intersections, parabolic closures and the dynamics of non-clique Artin groups. The membership-algorithm corollary is not part of it.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result proves the equivalent statement that its universal cover is contractible.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem, the K(π, 1) conjecture: the universal cover of the Salvetti complex is contractible for every Coxeter matrix on a finite set.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves quasi-isometric recognition of virtually polycyclic groups: every finitely generated group quasi-isometric to a finitely generated virtually polycyclic group is itself virtually polycyclic. It also realizes a finite-index subgroup of the recognized group as a uniform lattice in a simply connected solvable Lie group, which may differ from the original ambient group.
rows.explanation: States the main recognition theorem, its lattice corollary and the bounded-height theorem for self quasi-isometries of unimodular solvable Lie groups.

rows.scope_quote: The linked formalization proves the stronger coefficient-injectivity statement used in the paper: for any group $A$ and any relator in $A*\mathbb Z$ whose exponent sum in the cyclic generator is $1$ or $-1$, the natural map from $A$ into the quotient by that relator is injective. This is the selected unimodular-relator result underlying the conjecture.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: for every group A and every relator of exponent sum ±1 in the free generator, A injects into the one-relator quotient. Kervaire's conjecture is the paper's corollary of it.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result constructs a finite connected aspherical complex with a linear disk-filling bound whose fundamental group is word-hyperbolic but admits no geometric action on a nonempty proper complete $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ space. It also excludes locally $\mathrm{CAT}(-1)$ geodesic metrics on every finite complex homotopy equivalent to the witness. The stronger claims that the witness is two-dimensional and that those models admit no locally $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ metric are not included.
rows.explanation: States a finite aspherical complex with linear disk filling whose hyperbolic fundamental group has no geometric CAT(0) action, and excludes locally CAT(−1) metrics on homotopy-equivalent models. The main theorem also makes the complex two-dimensional and excludes locally CAT(0) metrics; those claims are not included.

rows.scope_quote: The Comparator also includes canonical Schwarzschild equality examples at every positive mass, with $m_{\mathrm{Bondi}}=m$ and enclosing area $16\pi m^2$. The paper's general Bondi–Penrose inequality for possibly disconnected weakly trapped boundaries remains unformalized.
rows.explanation: States the paper's end-replacement theorem (asymptotically flat ends replacing a hyperboloidal end, with masses approaching the Bondi mass and enclosing-area loss tending to zero) and Schwarzschild equality examples. The Bondi–Penrose inequality, which the note calls the paper's main inequality, is outside this statement.

rows.scope_quote: This selected statement identifies the spectral set. It does not assert the pure-point spectral type claimed in the accompanying paper.
rows.explanation: States only the almost-sure spectrum [−4 − h, 4 + h] of the planar Anderson operator, one clause of the main theorem that the note calls supporting. The pure-point spectral type and eigenbasis, the paper's claim, are not asserted.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result determines the sharp one-dimensional Lieb–Thirring constant for $1/2<\gamma<3/2$. For every nonnegative $W\in L^{\gamma+1/2}(\mathbb R)$, it bounds the full negative-eigenvalue moment of $-d^2/dx^2-W$ by the one-bound-state constant times the potential integral. This constant is optimal and is attained by $(r+1)\mathrm{sech}^2(rx)$, where $r=(\gamma-1/2)^{-1}$. No finite spectral cutoff is imposed.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: the sharp one-dimensional Lieb–Thirring constant for 1/2 < γ < 3/2, with optimality and equality at the explicit sech² potential.

rows.scope_quote: Let $I_m(Z)$ be the energy needed to remove $m$ electrons from a neutral atom of nuclear charge $Z$. There is a positive coefficient $a_{\mathrm{TF}}$ with the Thomas–Fermi variational characterization such that $I_m(Z)/m^{7/3}\to a_{\mathrm{TF}}$ whenever $m\to\infty$ and $Z/m\to\infty$, with integers $Z>m\ge1$. The corresponding iterated limsup and liminf limits hold with $Z\to\infty$ first. The energy uses the full antisymmetric Sobolev form domain; fixed-$m$ convergence and ground-state attainment are outside this statement.
rows.explanation: States the paper's generalised ionisation theorem: I_m(Z)/m^{7/3} → a_TF as m → ∞ with Z/m → ∞. The deficit theorem and ground-state attainment are not part of the statement.

rows.scope_quote:
For neutral Coulomb atoms with two electron spin states, the formalization proves the asymptotic law for generalized outer-electron radii defined by an expected exterior electron mass $m$. For every choice of normalized ground states, both the upper and lower large-nuclear-charge radius limits satisfy
$m^{1/3}R_m\longrightarrow (81\pi^2/2)^{1/3}$ as $m\to\infty$. The large-nuclear-charge limit is taken first. Ground states are inputs to the statement; their existence is not asserted separately.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the radii paper: m^{1/3}R_m → (81π²/2)^{1/3} for every choice of normalised neutral ground states, with the nuclear-charge limit first.

rows.scope_quote: This is a supporting Fourier cancellation statement. The paper's full character-sum vanishing theorem and its mutually unbiased bases bound are outside this selected statement.
rows.explanation: States a cancellation lemma for row ratios of order-six complex Hadamard matrices, a supporting step towards the Fourier vanishing theorem.

rows.scope_quote: The paper claims that at most three mutually unbiased orthonormal bases exist in $\mathbb C^6$. The linked formalization proves a weaker family bound: every family in its mutually unbiased bases model has at most five members. It also proves a Fourier character-sum vanishing statement for order-six complex Hadamard matrices not equivalent to the Tao matrix, uniformly over coordinate permutations.
rows.explanation: States a bound of five mutually unbiased bases in C⁶ where the main paper claims three, together with the Fourier vanishing theorem of the companion paper (whose no-complete-family theorem the bound of five also implies).

rows.scope_quote: There are absolute constants $\varepsilon_0,c_0>0$ such that, whenever the density $\rho$ and hard-sphere radius $a$ satisfy $\rho a^3<\varepsilon_0$, the condensate occupation fraction has limit inferior at least $c_0$ along every thermodynamic sequence with $N/L^3\to\rho$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem and its corollary: ground-state condensation with fraction at least c₀ in the dilute hard-sphere gas for every ground state and every state on the ground space. The positive-temperature result of the family's later paper is not part of it.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization includes the finite spherical $V_1$ bound of $1/100$ above the Laughlin state at flux $3(N-1)$ for all sufficiently large particle numbers $N$.
rows.explanation: States a uniform V₁ gap of 1/100 above the Laughlin state at flux 3(N − 1), whereas the paper's corollary gives 1/25; the Fock-space theorem itself is LaughlinFock.

rows.scope_quote: It also proves the stronger Fock-space inequality $H_Q^2\ge\gamma H_Q$ for every fixed $0<\gamma<\gamma_*$ and all sufficiently large fluxes $Q$, independently of particle number, where $\gamma_*=4616733319001/10^{14}>1/25$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the Fock-space paper: H_Q² ≥ γH_Q for every γ < γ* and all large Q, independently of particle number.

rows.scope_quote: This selected statement is the unperturbed Fock-space inequality. Stability under projected one-body potentials and uniqueness of the perturbed ground state are outside it.
rows.explanation: States the unperturbed gap inequality (V₁ energy at least 1/25 of the squared distance to the Laughlin line) that the stability paper uses as input; it coincides with the companion paper's corollary. Stability under disorder, the stability paper's main theorem, is outside it.

rows.scope_quote: For the untruncated planar model, the formalization proves the corresponding inequality at the endpoint $\gamma_*$ on every homogeneous particle sector. These statements use coefficient one for each pair projector.
rows.explanation: States the paper's planar corollary: the untruncated planar Hamiltonian satisfies the inequality at the endpoint γ* on every homogeneous sector.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves spontaneous magnetization for the nearest-neighbor isotropic quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet on $\mathbb Z^d$ for every $d\ge3$ and every spin $S\in\{\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\ldots\}$. At every sufficiently low positive temperature, it constructs a translation-invariant equilibrium state satisfying the KMS condition for the zero-field dynamics and having magnetization at least $S/4$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: for d ≥ 3, every spin S and all large β, a translation-invariant KMS state of the quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet with magnetisation at least S/4. The Bloch-law results of the family's later papers are not part of it.

rows.scope_quote: A separate trace-preserving PPT channel on $21\times21$ matrices has a square that is not entanglement breaking.
rows.explanation: States the paper's channel theorem: a trace-preserving PPT channel on 21 × 21 matrices whose square is not entanglement breaking. The note presents it as a consequence of the paper's construction; the zero-distillable-key theorem is outside it.

rows.scope_quote: The linked formalization covers these consequences: two explicitly specified PPT maps on $10\times10$ complex matrices have a composition that is not entanglement breaking, and the nonzero Choi matrix of that composition has no nonzero product vector in its range.
rows.explanation: States the paper's pair theorem: two explicit PPT maps on 10 × 10 matrices whose composition has a nonzero Choi matrix with no product vector in its range, so it is not entanglement breaking.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves the entropy photon-number inequality for two independent bosonic inputs with finite mean energy and any finite positive number $n$ of modes. Write $N(\rho)=g^{-1}(S(\rho)/n)$, where $S$ is von Neumann entropy and $g(x)=(x+1)\log(x+1)-x\log x$ is the thermal entropy per mode. For a beam splitter of transmissivity $0\le\eta\le1$, its output satisfies $N(\rho_C)\ge\eta N(\rho_A)+(1-\eta)N(\rho_B)$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: the entropy photon-number inequality for independent finite-energy bosonic inputs on any finite number of modes. The thermal-attenuator and broadcast consequences are outside it.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization rules out bounded-error parity computation by constant-depth quantum circuits with polynomially many zero-initialized ancillary qubits. For every fixed depth, polynomial bound on the total number of qubits, and $0<\varepsilon\le1/2$, every sufficiently large input length has an input on which the measured-output parity success probability is less than $1/2+\varepsilon$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: for every fixed depth, polynomial qubit bound and ε in (0, 1/2], constant-depth quantum circuits compute parity with success below 1/2 + ε on some input of every large length.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result supplies the polynomial-size parity consequence of the paper. For every fixed circuit depth and polynomial bound on the number of qubits, all sufficiently large input lengths have an input on which any such circuit computes measured-output parity with probability strictly below $2/3$. Ancillary qubits start at zero.
rows.explanation: States the case of success probability below 2/3 (ε = 1/6) of the parity theorem, which the note calls the polynomial-size consequence; the theorem itself covers every ε in (0, 1/2].

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves QMA-hardness of approximating the electronic Coulomb spectral infimum in three-dimensional continuum space when positive integer nuclear charges are encoded in binary. The instances have distinct rational nuclear positions and a unary electron count, and the energy ranges over antisymmetric continuum states and all spin sectors. A deterministic polynomial-time many-one reduction produces the promise gap with threshold separation at least one, while keeping the complete output length polynomial. The same Comparator file also contains the companion unit-charge result.
rows.explanation: The file states the main theorems of both papers: QMA-hardness of the continuum Coulomb ground energy with binary-encoded nuclear charges and with unit charges.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result determines the unassisted classical capacity of every generalized amplitude-damping channel with parameters in $[0,1]^2$. Its unrestricted Holevo information is additive across every number of repeated uses, equals an attained scalar maximum, and agrees with the operational capacity per use. Every maximizing equiprobable phase-pair product ensemble attains the corresponding block value. Additivity with an arbitrary different partner channel and decoding by separate measurements are not included.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: additivity of Holevo information and the classical capacity of every generalised amplitude-damping channel. Additivity with an arbitrary partner channel, the corollary, is not included.

rows.scope_quote: If its finite-dimensional entangled value is $v<1$, its answer sets are $A,B$, and $0<\delta<1-v$, then the probability of winning at least the fraction $v+\delta$ of $k$ repetitions is at most $\exp(-\kappa\delta^{13}k/(1+\log(|A||B|)))$ for one universal $\kappa>0$. The bound applies to every joint finite-dimensional strategy and to their supremum, without assuming attainment.
rows.explanation: States threshold parallel repetition with decay rate κδ^13/(1 + log(|A||B|)), whereas the main theorem gives κ₀δ^5/(1 + log d) with d = |A||B|; the paper notes that the δ^13 rate follows from its theorem.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization constructs a polynomial-time uniform quantum circuit family that outputs the complete prime factorization of every integer $N\ge2$ with probability exactly one. The circuits use one fixed finite set of bounded-arity gates, and both the gate count and number of qubits have polynomial worst-case bounds in the bit length of $N$. The probability-one conclusion is exact, rather than an asymptotic or bounded-error guarantee.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: a polynomial-time uniform quantum circuit family over a fixed finite gate set that outputs the prime factorisation of every N ≥ 2 with probability exactly one.

rows.scope_quote: The selected statement does not include complete rationality of the net, unitarizability of all simple modules, the braided tensor equivalence, or the classification of local extensions described in the paper.
rows.explanation: States the first parts of the main theorem: polynomial energy bounds, strong locality and an irreducible conformal net for a simple unitary strongly rational vertex operator algebra. Complete rationality, unitarisability of modules, the braided equivalence and the classification of extensions are outside it.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves that every admissible integrable minimizer of the zero-temperature Parisi functional for the pure zero-field Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model has full relative Stieltjes support on $[0,1)$. Equivalently, the order parameter increases strictly between every two overlap values below one, so its support has no gap. The covariance normalization is $\xi(t)=t^2/2$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the full-support paper: every admissible minimiser of the zero-temperature Parisi functional has support [0, 1), with the associated diffusion and moment identities.

rows.scope_quote: It also proves convergence of finite Gaussian coefficient sums to the curvature integral, which approaches the ground-state value as the terminal time tends to one. The selected statement covers these value and approximation results; it does not itself assert convergence of QAOA circuit energies.
rows.explanation: States variational identities for the SK ground-state energy used in the QAOA argument, conditional on an admissible Parisi minimiser. It does not assert convergence of QAOA energies, the main theorem.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves that interpolated free group factors with any parameters $r,s>1$, including the infinite parameter, are normally trace-preservingly isomorphic. The paper's fundamental-group conclusion is a further consequence rather than a separate selected statement here.
rows.explanation: States that all interpolated free group factors L(F_r), 1 < r ≤ ∞, are isomorphic, which contains the main theorem L(F₂) ≅ L(F₃) and the rank-step theorem.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves this for arbitrary Hilbert spaces. It also gives one universal hyperreflexivity constant for all unital von Neumann algebras.
rows.explanation: States the main similarity theorem for every unital C*-algebra and Hilbert space, together with the uniform commutator estimate and universal hyperreflexivity.

rows.scope_quote: The linked commutator estimate is uniform over all finite matrix amplifications: its constant is independent of the algebra, Hilbert space, and amplification size. This is the quantitative derivation estimate supporting the similarity result.
rows.explanation: States the uniform amplified commutator estimate, which the paper states as a theorem in its introduction and the note describes as the estimate supporting the similarity result; similarity itself is KadisonSimilarity.

rows.scope_quote: For every $\varepsilon>0$, there is a $\delta>0$ such that any two unital von Neumann algebras on the same complex Hilbert space at Kadison–Kastler distance below $\delta$ are conjugate by a unitary $u$ with $\lVert u-1\rVert<\varepsilon$. The tolerance depends only on $\varepsilon$, uniformly over the algebras, their representations, and the Hilbert space.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: von Neumann algebras close in Kadison–Kastler distance are conjugate by a unitary near the identity, with δ depending only on ε.

rows.scope_quote: For a faithful normal state with scalar centralizer in the stated standard-space representation, the formalized result converts positive modular spectral averages into uniformly bounded algebra elements. Given unit vectors in shrinking spectral bands around a real number $s$ and a positive limiting symmetric average for a bounded operator $T$, it finds a subsequence of bounded algebra elements whose images under $T$ stay uniformly nonzero and whose spectral bands have four times the original widths. The absolute bicentralizer conjecture is not included.
rows.explanation: States the bounded-recovery theorem for modular spectral averages (a theorem in Section 4 of the paper), a step towards the main theorem. The bicentraliser theorem BC(M, φ) = C1, the paper's main result, is not included.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves that real rank zero of the uniform tracial ultrapower of the uniform tracial completion implies uniform property $\Gamma$ for a simple separable unital infinite-dimensional nuclear stably finite $C^*$-algebra with traces. The conclusion holds at every specified free ultrafilter under the corresponding real-rank-zero hypothesis.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem (tracial real rank zero implies uniform property Γ) and the paper's comparison theorems giving Jiang–Su absorption under strict comparison and in the stated stably projectionless case.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization constructs an explicit separable unital full group $C^*$-algebra that has no unital embedding into $B^\omega$ for any nonzero unital nuclear $C^*$-algebra $B$ and any free ultrafilter $\omega$ on $\mathbb N$. In particular, it does not embed unitally into an ultrapower of the Cuntz algebra $\mathcal O_2$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: the full group C*-algebra of Z[1/2]³ ⋊ (SL₃(Z) × Z) embeds unitally in no norm ultrapower of a nonzero unital nuclear algebra, in particular not in one of O₂.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization for the companion paper [Backward intertwiners and a transitive commutant](../../preprints/Backward-intertwiners-and-a-transitive-commutant-September-27-2026/paper.pdf) gives, on every separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, a nonzero quasinilpotent operator whose commutant is transitive, proper, and closed in the strong operator topology. Thus no nontrivial closed subspace is invariant under every operator in the commutant.
rows.explanation: States the backward-intertwiner paper's corollary (a quasinilpotent operator with transitive commutant on every separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space) rather than its direct-model theorem.

rows.scope_quote: The linked statements also include an earlier existence construction, a product realization, and the selected product model's Brown measure $\delta_0$.
rows.explanation: States the invariant-projection counterexample for some irrational angle, whereas the main theorem gives one for every irrational angle; the note calls it an earlier existence construction.

rows.scope_quote: The linked statements also include an earlier existence construction, a product realization, and the selected product model's Brown measure $\delta_0$.
rows.explanation: States only that some II₁ factor with separable predual contains a nonzero quasinilpotent operator without nontrivial invariant projections, an existential form of the main theorem without its prescribed rotation and weight.

rows.scope_quote: The hyperinvariant-subspace problem asks whether every bounded operator on a complex Hilbert space has a nontrivial closed subspace invariant under every operator that commutes with it. The formalization gives a negative answer on every separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space: there is a nonzero quasinilpotent operator with a transitive commutant. Its commutant is a proper unital operator algebra closed in the strong operator topology. The construction therefore has no nonzero proper closed hyperinvariant subspace.
rows.explanation: States the corollary shared by both accompanying papers: every separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space carries a nonzero quasinilpotent operator with a transitive, proper, strongly closed commutant, hence no nontrivial hyperinvariant subspace.

rows.scope_quote: For every irrational rotation angle $\theta\in(0,1)$, the formalization constructs a continuous nonnegative circle weight with a single zero and logarithmic integral $-\infty$ whose weighted rotation is nonzero and quasinilpotent. In its associated hyperfinite type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor, the operator has no nontrivial invariant projection: $(1-p)Tp=0$ forces $p=0$ or $p=1$. The linked statements also include an earlier existence construction, a product realization, and the selected product model's Brown measure $\delta_0$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem for every irrational rotation angle (a continuous weight whose weighted rotation is nonzero, quasinilpotent and without nontrivial invariant projection), with the product realisation.

rows.scope_quote: The linked statements also include an earlier existence construction, a product realization, and the selected product model's Brown measure $\delta_0$.
rows.explanation: States that the Brown measure of the selected product weighted shift is the point mass at zero, a property of the paper's product model rather than its main theorem.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization constructs a separable $C^*$-algebra with normalized $2$-quasitraces and fixed positive contractions $a,b$ for which every such quasitrace satisfies $\mathrm{Re}(\tau(a+b)-\tau(a)-\tau(b))\ge1/144$. Thus none is additive on this pair.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem with its constant: a separable C*-algebra with positive contractions a, b on which every normalised 2-quasitrace has τ(a + b) − τ(a) − τ(b) ≥ 1/144.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization also gives simple stably finite $C^*$-algebras whose spatial tensor product is properly infinite, a separable stably finite algebra with no tracial state, and a tensor-product example in which normalized $2$-quasitraces are lost. These are the stable-finiteness consequences named in the paper's title.
rows.explanation: States the paper's corollary on tensor products: stably finite algebras with properly infinite tensor product, a stably finite algebra without tracial states, and loss of quasitraces.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves vanishing of bounded Hochschild cohomology in every degree at least two for a complex von Neumann algebra with coefficients in itself. Every bounded multilinear cocycle of such a degree is the Hochschild differential of a bounded multilinear cochain one degree lower. No separability or type restriction is imposed. The degree-one inner-derivation theorem is outside this selected statement.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: bounded Hochschild cohomology of every von Neumann algebra with coefficients in itself vanishes in each degree k ≥ 2. The degree-one theorem is outside the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization answers the generator problem affirmatively for type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors with separable predual: one bounded operator generates the factor under adjoints and weak-operator closure. It imposes no separability assumption on the representing Hilbert space or on the operator-norm topology.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: every type II₁ factor with separable predual is generated by one operator.

rows.scope_quote: It also proves the paper's relative-generation result. For an irreducible inclusion of type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors with separable predual for the larger factor, the unitaries that generate the larger factor together with the smaller one form a dense $G_\delta$ set in the normalized trace two-norm topology. The normalized faithful normal trace is included in the assertion.
rows.explanation: States the relative-generation theorem: for an irreducible inclusion of II₁ factors, the unitaries generating the larger factor with the smaller one form a dense G_δ set.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization gives a counterexample in ZFC: a unital infinite-dimensional simple complex $C^*$-algebra with a faithful tracial state has that uniqueness property for irreducible representations but is not isomorphic to the compact operators on any Hilbert space. No additional set-theoretic assumption is used.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem in ZFC: a unital infinite-dimensional simple C*-algebra with a faithful tracial state, one irreducible representation up to equivalence, and not isomorphic to compact operators. Seven definitions are Comparator holes; their library bodies match the challenge file.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization disproves equality of microstates and nonmicrostates free entropy even when both quantities are finite. It constructs a bounded self-adjoint tuple $X$ in a von Neumann algebra with a faithful normal tracial state such that $-\infty<\chi(X)\le\chi^*(X)-1/2<\infty$. Here $\chi$ is the microstates entropy with an operator-norm cutoff and a limsup over matrix sizes, and $\chi^*$ is the nonmicrostates entropy defined using free semicircular noise. The example has a fixed finite number of variables.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: a bounded self-adjoint tuple with −∞ < χ(X) ≤ χ*(X) − 1/2 < ∞, separating the two free entropies.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result proves that, for every nonzero unital separable complex $C^*$-algebra $A$ and every free ultrafilter on $\mathbb N$, the norm central-sequence algebra has no nonzero character exactly when $A\cong A\otimes_{\min}\mathcal Z$. No nuclearity, simplicity, trace, or comparison hypothesis is imposed.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: for nonzero unital separable A and every free ultrafilter, the central-sequence algebra has no characters exactly when A absorbs the Jiang–Su algebra. The finite and infinite tensor-power results are not part of the statement.

rows.scope_quote: For each closed ideal $I$, it also constructs the trace that is zero on positive elements of $I$ and infinite elsewhere. These traces are exactly the additive idempotents, meaning $\tau+\tau=\tau$, and their addition recovers ideal inclusion. Spatial classification, existence of the stabilization models, norm uniqueness, and final intertwining are outside this supporting comparison.
rows.explanation: States the transport of ideals under trace-cone equivalences and the description of ideal traces as additive idempotents, one of the five supporting comparisons named in the Comparator README. The classification theorem itself is outside it.

rows.scope_quote: For exact algebras, proper infiniteness of one fixed finite amplification of every positive element already implies individual proper infiniteness and strong pure infiniteness.
rows.explanation: States the paper's exact-algebra theorem: proper infiniteness of one fixed amplification of every positive element gives strong pure infiniteness. The O∞-absorption corollary is not part of the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves that a complex $C^*$-algebra in which every positive element is properly infinite is strongly purely infinite, with the full positive-element diagonalization property. No exactness, nuclearity, unitality, or simplicity assumption is needed for this implication.
rows.explanation: States the paper's theorem that individual proper infiniteness of positive elements implies strong pure infiniteness, with no exactness or nuclearity assumption.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization constructs a counterexample from a coarse disjoint union of finite connected graphs with uniformly bounded degree. Its degree-one coarse $K$-homology contains an infinite-order class whose image under ordinary coarse assembly into the reduced locally compact Roe algebra vanishes. The class remains nonzero after tensoring with $\mathbb Q$, so rational injectivity fails.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: a bounded-geometry coarse union of finite graphs with a rationally nonzero K-homology class killed by coarse assembly, so the coarse Novikov conjecture fails. The maximal-assembly result of the family's later paper is not part of it.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result is the elementary-expansion theorem used in this approach: for every Grothendieck coherator in the Ara–Henry convention and every boundary-cellular model, attaching an $(n+1)$-disk along its source $n$-face induces a weak equivalence.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem, the elementary-expansion weak equivalence for every Grothendieck coherator. The semi-model structure and the homotopy-hypothesis comparison with spaces, corollaries in Section 5, are not included.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves the higher-dimensional Thomason model-structure theorem for small strict globular $n$-categories in every positive finite dimension and in dimension $\omega$. Each category has the stated proper combinatorial model structure, Quillen equivalent to simplicial sets through the twice-subdivided categorification and twice-extended Street nerve adjunction.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: proper combinatorial Thomason model structures on strict n-categories for every n ≥ 1 and n = ω, Quillen equivalent to simplicial sets, with weak equivalences detected by the Street nerve.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result gives a unique surjective real-linear isometric extension for arbitrary nonzero real Banach spaces, with no finite-dimensionality, separability, reflexivity, or convexity assumptions. For complex spaces viewed as real spaces, the conclusion is real linearity rather than complex linearity.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: every surjective isometry between unit spheres of nonzero real Banach spaces extends uniquely to a real-linear isometry, by the radial formula.

rows.scope_quote: This is the conditional counterexample direction. The positive consistency direction and the paper's full relative-independence conclusions are outside the selected statement.
rows.explanation: States the continuum-hypothesis direction of the main theorem: under CH there is an infinite-dimensional Banach space, real or complex, with no infinite-dimensional separable quotient. The positive consistency direction and the independence corollary are outside it.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result constructs one separable real Banach space $X$ that is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to $X\times c_0$ but contains no closed linear subspace isomorphic to $c_0$. The same space contains a bi-Lipschitz copy of $c_0$, is bi-Lipschitz universal for separable metric spaces, and is not linearly isomorphic to $X\times c_0$. Thus nonlinear absorption of $c_0$ does not force a linear copy of it.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the absorption paper: a separable Banach space bi-Lipschitz equivalent to its sum with c₀ that contains no linear copy of c₀.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized counterexample gives separable real Banach spaces $X,Y$ that are bi-Lipschitz equivalent but not linearly isomorphic. The bijection has lower Lipschitz bound $4/21$ and upper bound $76/25$. The linear obstruction is explicit: $X$ contains a linear isometric copy of $c_0(\ell_2)$, whereas $Y$ contains no bounded linear copy of that space.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: separable Banach spaces X, Y with a bi-Lipschitz bijection (constants 4/21 and 76/25) that are not linearly isomorphic.

rows.scope_quote: The complete Crouzeix inequality bounds a matrix-valued polynomial evaluated at a matrix by its maximum norm on the numerical range. The formalized result proves the bound with constant $2$ for every positive matrix and coefficient size, every polynomial degree, and arbitrary complex coefficients. It also proves that no smaller universal constant works. Normality of the matrix and nonempty interior of its numerical range are not assumed.
rows.explanation: States the same complete Crouzeix inequality with constant 2 and its optimality as DirectCrouzeix, in a separately written statement; it is also the polynomial corollary of the structural paper.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves the complete Crouzeix inequality with sharp constant two for every bounded operator on an arbitrary complex Hilbert space. For every matrix-valued polynomial, its operator evaluation has norm at most twice its supremum norm on the numerical range. The same bound holds for finite matrix-valued functions holomorphic near the closure of the numerical range and for rational functions with poles outside that closure. No separability assumption is required.
rows.explanation: States the complete Crouzeix inequality with sharp constant 2 for every bounded operator on every complex Hilbert space, the structural paper's Hilbert-space corollary; it contains the direct paper's matrix theorem.

rows.scope_quote: The complete Crouzeix inequality bounds a matrix-valued polynomial evaluated at a matrix by its maximum norm on the numerical range. The formalized result proves the bound with constant $2$ for every positive matrix and coefficient size, every polynomial degree, and arbitrary complex coefficients. It also proves that no smaller universal constant works. Normality of the matrix and nonempty interior of its numerical range are not assumed.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the direct-proof paper: the complete Crouzeix inequality with constant 2 for matrix-valued polynomials of every size, with sharpness of the constant.

rows.scope_quote: The linked supporting statements include numerical-range geometry and finite-compression identities.
rows.explanation: States supporting numerical-range geometry and finite-compression statements used for the Hilbert-space theorem.

rows.scope_quote: For finite matrices in a bounded convex domain with regular real-analytic Jordan boundary, the structural result gives an attained optimal similarity with condition number at most two and one continuous positive boundary density of mass the identity representing every matrix-valued analytic test. The linked supporting statements include numerical-range geometry and finite-compression identities.
rows.explanation: States the structural paper's main theorems: an attained optimal similarity with condition number at most two and a common positive boundary representation, for admissible domains.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result establishes this equivalence for every nonzero real Banach space with the approximation property: $X$ is $K$-convex exactly when both $X$ and $X^*$ have finite cotype.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: a nonzero real Banach space with the approximation property is K-convex exactly when it and its dual have finite cotype.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result proves that a real Banach space has nontrivial Markov type exactly when it admits an equivalent uniformly convex norm, hence exactly when it is superreflexive. Nontrivial Markov type means a uniform Markov-type bound for some exponent $p>1$ over all finite stationary reversible chains and all positive times. The exponent and equivalent norm may depend on the space, and the zero space is included. Additional formalized consequences concern uniformly smooth renormings and reflexivity of finitely representable spaces.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem (nontrivial Markov type forces superreflexivity) as an equivalence with having an equivalent uniformly convex norm.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result gives an affirmative answer: every nonexpansive self-map of a nonempty closed bounded convex subset of a real reflexive Banach space has a fixed point in the original norm. Zero and nonseparable spaces are included, with no uniform convexity, normal structure, or weak-continuity assumption.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: every nonexpansive self-map of a nonempty closed bounded convex subset of a real reflexive Banach space has a fixed point. The commuting-family corollary is not part of the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result disproves such a comparison: for every $a,b\ge1$, there is an origin-symmetric convex body $K$ in a positive finite dimension with $\log N(K,B_\infty)>b\log N(B_\infty^\circ,a^{-1}K^\circ)$, where $N$ is the least number of translates in a finite cover. A further construction makes the dual-to-primal logarithmic entropy ratio tend to zero as the dimension grows.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: for every a, b ≥ 1 a symmetric convex body violating the metric-entropy duality comparison with those constants.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization constructs a countable metric space with all distinct points at distance at least one whose real Lipschitz-free space has the approximation property but fails every bounded approximation bound. The metric space is unbounded and not proper.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: a countable uniformly discrete metric space whose Lipschitz-free space has the approximation property but no bounded approximation property.

rows.scope_quote: The earlier quantitative renorming result for real $\ell_1$ is retained: for each integer $p\ge1$, an equivalent complete norm has the $2B_p$-bounded approximation property but fails the $p$-bounded approximation property, where $B_p=300p^2+150p+5$.
rows.explanation: States the paper's renorming corollary for real ℓ₁ (an equivalent norm with the 2B_p-bounded but not the p-bounded approximation property), which the note calls the earlier quantitative result.

rows.scope_quote: The paper constructs Banach spaces from bounded tree potentials and path costs to separate averaged midpoint convexity from asymptotic uniform convexity. For the specified tree-potential completions, the formalization proves completeness, separability, infinite dimension, and an averaged midpoint modulus of at least $\sqrt{1+t^2/4}-1$ for $0<t<1$. No space linearly isomorphic to one of these completions is asymptotically uniformly convex.
rows.explanation: States the tree-potential paper's main theorem: complete separable infinite-dimensional spaces with averaged midpoint modulus at least √(1 + t²/4) − 1 and no AUC renorming.

rows.scope_quote: The paper exhibits a real $L_1$ subspace with positive averaged midpoint convexity but no equivalent asymptotically uniformly convex norm. For every closed infinite-dimensional subspace whose unit ball is precompact in measure and which has the Daugavet property, the formalization computes the moduli at every unit vector: the averaged midpoint modulus is $\max(t/2,t-1)$ and the usual one-sided asymptotic modulus is $\max(0,t-2)$ for every $t>0$. The same formulas hold after taking the infimum over unit vectors, and every equivalent norm fails asymptotic uniform convexity.
rows.explanation: States the Daugavet paper's main theorem (exact averaged midpoint and asymptotic moduli for the stated subspaces of L¹) and constructs an example satisfying its hypotheses.

rows.scope_quote: The paper studies embeddings of countably branching diamond graphs into Banach spaces built from tree segments. The formalization proves that every embedding of the depth-$k$ diamond with distortion $D$, at any positive scale, satisfies $1+k/4\le D^2$ in either of two spaces: the full dual of the completed finite-height forest space and the closed coordinate span in the dual of the infinite-tree space. The bound applies to all pairs of vertices and is unconditional.
rows.explanation: States the diamond-distortion paper's main theorem: every distortion-D embedding of the depth-k diamond satisfies D² ≥ 1 + k/4 in either space.

rows.scope_quote: The paper constructs a Banach space whose midpoint geometry is asymptotically uniformly convex even though no equivalent norm is asymptotically uniformly convex in the usual one-sided sense. The formalization proves that the full dual of the specified segment-norm completion is infinite-dimensional, separable, and reflexive; its averaged midpoint modulus is at least $\sqrt{1+t^2/12}-1$ for every $t>0$, while every equivalent norm fails asymptotic uniform convexity. It also proves that an embedding of a depth-$k$ countably branching diamond has distortion at least $\sqrt{1+k/12}$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the reflexive tree-space paper: the dual J* is infinite-dimensional, separable and reflexive with no AUC renorming, with the midpoint modulus bound and diamond distortion at least √(1 + k/12).

rows.scope_quote: The paper forms a real $L_1$ space from the closed span of products of independent multipliers along tree paths. For a positive, nonconstant multiplier of mean one and finite second moment, the formalization proves that this space is infinite-dimensional and has no equivalent asymptotically uniformly convex norm.
rows.explanation: States the independent-products paper's main theorem: the spaces X_W have no equivalent AUC norm, with the explicit midpoint-modulus lower bounds for exponential and Gaussian-square multipliers.

rows.scope_quote: The paper controls midpoint lenses in Banach spaces defined by tree-segment norms. The formalization proves the following estimate in both the full dual of the finite-height forest space and the coordinate predual of the infinite-tree space. If $x$ is supported on a finite ancestral set $H$, $R\ge0$, and $\|x+y\|,\|x-y\|\le R$, then the part of $y$ outside $H$ has norm at most $2\sqrt{R^2-\|x\|^2}$.
rows.explanation: States the midpoint-lens paper's main tail estimate in both the finite-height forest dual and the infinite-tree predual.

rows.scope_quote: The paper constructs three Banach spaces from recursive tree potentials: a root-sum space, a zero-root space, and a joined space. The formalization proves that all three are infinite-dimensional and have no equivalent asymptotically uniformly convex norm. The root-sum and joined spaces have averaged midpoint modulus at least $t^3/128$ for $0<t<1$, and the root-sum modulus is positive for every $t>0$. The zero-root estimate retains its finite ancestral support and tail hypotheses, and the zero-root and joined spaces are reflexive.
rows.explanation: States the recursive-potential paper's main theorem (midpoint modulus at least t³/128 for the root-sum and joined spaces, with no AUC renorming) together with its separated-family and variable-exponent results.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves that every closed smooth Riemannian surface admits a smooth isometric immersion into $\mathbb R^4$. The differential preserves the Riemannian inner product on every tangent space. No orientability assumption is imposed, and the statement asks for an immersion rather than an embedding.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: every closed smooth Riemannian surface admits a smooth isometric immersion into R⁴.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized counterexample is a smooth positive-definite metric on $(-1,1)^2$ for which no neighborhood of the origin admits a smooth isometric immersion into $\mathbb R^3$. The obstruction applies to every smooth candidate map on every such neighborhood.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: a smooth metric on (−1, 1)² such that no neighbourhood of the origin admits a smooth isometric immersion into R³.

rows.scope_quote: A second statement proves that this coefficient is optimal by giving, in Euclidean space, a cycle for which every compactly supported integral filling has at least that mass. This yields the selected integral-current form of the Cartan–Hadamard isoperimetric conjecture.
rows.explanation: States the optimality clause of the main theorem: a Euclidean cycle every integral filling of which has at least the stated mass. The filling inequality itself is SharpCAT0Filling.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves the sharp Euclidean filling inequality for every compactly supported integral $n$-cycle in a proper $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ space, for $n\ge2$. It constructs a compactly supported integral filling whose mass is at most $C_n$ times the boundary mass to the power $(n+1)/n$, where $C_n$ is the Euclidean isoperimetric coefficient. Integer multiplicities and the ambient dimension are unrestricted.
rows.explanation: States the sharp filling inequality of the main theorem for integral cycles in every proper CAT(0) space. The theorem's final clause, optimality of the coefficient, is the separate statement FillingCoefficient.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result establishes this for every closed connected smooth four-manifold, keeping the almost-complex structure fixed. No integrability assumption or prescribed cohomology class for the compatible form is required.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem (of the current edition of the paper the note links): on a closed connected four-manifold, an almost-complex structure tamed by a symplectic form admits a compatible one. The cone results are not part of the statement.

rows.scope_quote:
The formalization proves Siegel and Yao's ball-packing criterion in every symplectic dimension $2n$ with $n\ge3$. For $k\ge1$ closed standard balls of positive capacities $R_1,\ldots,R_k$, disjoint symplectic embeddings into the interior of a ball of capacity $R$ exist exactly when
$\sum_i R_i^n<R^n$ and $R_i+R_j<R$ for all $i\ne j$.
Capacity is $\pi$ times squared Euclidean radius, and each embedding is defined on a neighborhood of its closed source ball. The linked statements include both the full equivalence and the necessity direction.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: in dimension 2n ≥ 6, balls pack symplectically into a ball exactly when the volume and pairwise capacity inequalities hold.

rows.scope_quote: The linked statements include both the full equivalence and the necessity direction.
rows.explanation: States only the necessity direction of the packing criterion (a packing forces the volume and pairwise inequalities); the sufficiency direction is in BallPacking.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized counterexample is a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of the complex quadric threefold with exactly three fixed points, while every smooth function on that manifold has at least four critical points. At least one fixed point is degenerate. The separate nondegenerate Morse-number construction is not included.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of the complex quadric threefold with exactly three fixed points, fewer than the four critical points every smooth function has. The nondegenerate construction of a companion paper is not included.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization classifies connected smooth closed Einstein four-manifolds with strictly positive sectional curvature. Up to positive scaling and isometry, every such manifold is the round four-sphere, the complex projective plane with its Fubini–Study metric, or round real projective four-space. No orientability hypothesis is required. In the oriented case, only the sphere and complex projective plane occur.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: closed Einstein four-manifolds of positive sectional curvature are, up to scaling and isometry, S⁴, CP² with the Fubini–Study metric or RP⁴.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves the upper bound on every fixed smooth closed connected Riemannian surface: there is a surface-dependent constant $C$ such that the one-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the zero set of every nonzero real eigenfunction with $\lambda>0$ is at most $C\sqrt\lambda$. The known lower bound is not part of this selected statement.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: on every closed smooth surface, nodal length of an eigenfunction is at most C√λ.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized results contradict Yau's proposed $O(\sqrt\lambda)$ upper bound for nodal measure in dimensions three and four. On $S^3$, every prescribed smooth neighborhood of the round metric contains one fixed smooth metric with an eigenfunction sequence of unbounded nodal-measure ratio. A second fixed metric on $S^2\times T^2$ has the same property. In both cases the eigenvalues tend to infinity and the intrinsic nodal measures are finite.
rows.explanation: States both main theorems of the counterexample paper: metrics on S³ near the round metric and on S² × T² with eigenfunction sequences whose nodal-measure ratio to √λ is unbounded.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized counterexample fixes one smooth metric on $S^4\times S^1$ and a sequence of nonzero smooth eigenfunctions whose positive eigenvalues tend to infinity, while the intrinsic four-dimensional nodal measures divided by the square roots of the eigenvalues tend to infinity. The metric is fixed throughout the sequence.
rows.explanation: States a fixed metric on S⁴ × S¹ with nodal measure divided by √λ tending to infinity, whereas the main theorem gives a power-law violation, with nodal measure divided by λ^{1/2+ε₀} tending to infinity for a fixed ε₀ > 0.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves the Euclidean-complete affine Bernstein theorem for graph dimensions $3\le n\le9$. If a smooth function on a nonempty open convex domain has positive-definite Hessian, satisfies the affine maximal equation, and its graph is complete in the induced Euclidean metric, then the domain is all of $\mathbb R^n$ and the function is a positive-definite quadratic polynomial plus an affine term. Its graph is therefore an elliptic paraboloid.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: for 3 ≤ n ≤ 9, Euclidean-complete affine maximal graphs are elliptic paraboloids. The extension to immersed hypersurfaces is outside the statement.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization determines the isoperimetric profile and all minimizers in the unit cubic flat three-torus. At every volume $0<V<1$, a minimizer exists, and the minimizers, up to null-set changes, are exactly balls, circular tubes about shortest closed geodesics, coordinate slabs, and their complements in the appropriate volume ranges.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: the isoperimetric profile of the unit cubic flat three-torus with all minimisers (balls, tubes, slabs and complements) and the equality cases.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization transfers a weak Hessian upper bound to every prescribed minimizing geodesic in an $\mathrm{RCD}(K,N)$ space with finite $N>1$. If a bounded globally Lipschitz function $F$ has weak Hessian bounded above by $G$ times the metric, where $G$ is bounded and continuous, then every constant-speed geodesic $\gamma:[0,1]\to X$ satisfies $(F\circ\gamma)''\le G(\gamma)\,d(\gamma(0),\gamma(1))^2$ in the distributional sense.
rows.explanation: States the paper's main theorem: in RCD(K, N) spaces a weak Hessian upper bound controls the second distributional derivative along every constant-speed geodesic. Gigli's characterisation of the family's other paper is not part of it.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result separates absence of conjugate points from nonpositive sectional curvature. It constructs a closed connected orientable smooth three-manifold with a smooth Riemannian metric having no conjugate points, while the same manifold admits no smooth metric of everywhere nonpositive sectional curvature. The no-conjugate-points assertion ranges over all geodesics and tangent-bundle Jacobi fields, including constant geodesics and unbounded time intervals. The separate no-focal-points and CAT(0) consequences are not included.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: a closed orientable three-manifold with a metric without conjugate points that admits no metric of nonpositive curvature. The no-focal-points and CAT(0) consequences are not included.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result constructs a nonempty contractible complex threefold with a complete Kähler metric whose real sectional curvatures lie between two fixed negative constants. Nevertheless, it has no system of bounded holomorphic coordinates and is not biholomorphic to a bounded domain. The metric is obtained from an explicitly controlled potential. This is the negatively pinched construction; the different companion with only one-sided curvature control is separate.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: a contractible complex threefold with a complete Kähler metric of negatively pinched sectional curvature that has no bounded holomorphic coordinates.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result gives uniform bi-Hölder optimal transport for squared-distance cost on each fixed compact connected smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension at least two satisfying weak MTW. For probability densities between fixed positive lower and finite upper bounds, one exponent and constant work for every pair of densities. The optimal map is a homeomorphism, is unique almost everywhere, and both it and its inverse satisfy the global Hölder bound. The constants are uniform over the density class on the fixed manifold, not over varying metrics.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the transport paper: uniform bi-Hölder optimal maps for squared-distance cost between densities with fixed bounds under weak MTW.

rows.scope_quote: On a compact connected smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension at least two, the formalized result proves that weak MTW curvature implies convexity of every open tangent injectivity domain. Prior convexity or nonfocality is not assumed.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: weak MTW curvature implies convexity of every open tangent injectivity domain on a compact manifold of dimension at least two. The paper's arbitrary-potential local-injectivity assertion is not covered.

rows.scope_quote: It constructs one complete smooth metric with nonnegative Ricci curvature on an even-dimensional Euclidean space, Euclidean near the origin and with asymptotic volume ratio strictly between zero and one, admitting more independent harmonic functions of the prescribed growth degree than the Euclidean count. The construction uses dimension $16$ and degree $50000$. Separate tangent-cone and cone-spectrum conclusions are not included.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem with an explicit witness (dimension 16, degree 50000): a complete metric with nonnegative Ricci curvature on R^n with more harmonic functions of degree-k growth than Euclidean space. The challenge file states the claim through a placeholder axiom; Comparator admits only the three standard axioms in the library proof.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result gives global existence and uniqueness for the three-dimensional one-species relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell system. The initial particle density is nonnegative, smooth, and compactly supported; the initial fields have bounded derivatives of all orders, finite energy, and satisfy both Gauss constraints. The solution is smooth on every finite time interval, has compact particle phase support there, and is unique among classical solutions. No smallness, symmetry, or neutrality assumption is imposed.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: global existence and uniqueness of classical solutions of the three-dimensional relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell system for smooth compactly supported data, with no smallness assumption.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves nonuniqueness for the periodic hard-sphere Boltzmann equation by constructing two distinct global renormalized solutions on $\mathbb T^3\times\mathbb R^3$ with the same nonnegative initial density. The data have bounded velocity support and finite mass, energy, and absolute entropy. Both solutions conserve local mass and total momentum and satisfy the global energy and entropy-dissipation inequalities.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: two distinct global renormalised solutions of the periodic hard-sphere Boltzmann equation with the same initial density. The local-conservation refinements of the family's later paper are outside it.

rows.scope_quote: The formalized result gives nonuniqueness for bounded measurable scalar conductivities on the ball $B(0,3)\subset\mathbb R^3$: two uniformly positive conductivities differ on a set of positive volume, equal $1$ near the boundary, and have the same full weak Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator. Weak solutions exist uniquely for every boundary trace.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: two bounded measurable scalar conductivities on a ball, equal to 1 near the boundary and different on a set of positive volume, with the same Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. The localised corollary is not included.

rows.scope_quote: The linked formalization proves the existence side: in dimension seven there is a nonzero one-homogeneous global minimizer that is not a half-space solution.
rows.explanation: States the existence half of the main theorem: a nonflat one-homogeneous global minimiser in dimension seven. Flatness in dimensions at most six and the singular-set corollary are outside it.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves the stronger interior statement on every nonempty smooth bounded simply connected planar domain: every nonzero eigenfunction in the first positive Neumann eigenspace has nonvanishing gradient throughout the interior. Consequently all global maxima and minima lie on the boundary. The conclusion applies to every eigenfunction even when the eigenvalue is multiple.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: first nonconstant Neumann eigenfunctions on smooth bounded simply connected planar domains have no interior critical points, so their extrema lie on the boundary.

rows.scope_quote: For $n\ge2$, $p,q>0$, and real $A,B$ with $(n+A)/(p+1)+(n+B)/(q+1)>n-2$, there are no positive functions, continuous everywhere and $C^2$ off the origin, satisfying $-\Delta u=|x|^A v^p$ and $-\Delta v=|x|^B u^q$ away from the origin. It includes the globally $C^2$ unweighted case for $n\ge3$. The critical equality case is not included.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: nonexistence of positive solutions of the subcritical Hénon–Lane–Emden system, including the unweighted corollary. The critical case is not included.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization constructs stable self-similar finite-time blowup for defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equations on the twelve-dimensional torus. For every prescribed lower bound on the power, it selects an odd power at least that large and a Sobolev index $k>8$ for which a nonempty open set of $H^k$ initial data has the stated classical blowup behavior. The selected quantifier gives arbitrarily large odd powers, rather than every sufficiently large odd power.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem (an open set of H^k data with stable self-similar blowup for the defocusing equation on the twelve-torus, for arbitrarily large odd powers) and the Gaussian corollary. The Schrödinger flow and two Sobolev operations are Comparator holes filled from OpenAI's library.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves global uniqueness in the three-dimensional static isotropic elasticity inverse problem. On a bounded connected smooth domain, let two pairs of smooth real Lamé moduli satisfy $\mu>0$ and $3\lambda+2\mu>0$ on the closure. If their full displacement-to-traction maps agree, then both Lamé moduli agree throughout the domain. The selected statement is uniqueness; it does not supply a reconstruction algorithm.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: the displacement-to-traction map determines smooth isotropic Lamé moduli on a bounded smooth domain in R³.

rows.scope_quote: For the three-marginal Coulomb cost in $\mathbb R^3$, the formalization constructs a smooth compactly supported probability density, with smooth compactly supported square root, for which no pair of measure-preserving Borel maps attains the Kantorovich minimum.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem: a smooth compactly supported density for which no pair of measure-preserving maps attains the three-marginal Coulomb minimum, with equality of the Monge and Kantorovich infima. The inverse-power extensions are outside it.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves one-third Hölder stability of Brenier maps from the uniform measure on a compact convex body with nonempty interior in $\mathbb R^d$, for every $d\ge2$. For targets supported in one fixed nonempty compact set, the $L^2$ distance between the unique quadratic optimal maps is at most a constant times the one-third power of the targets' $2$-Wasserstein distance. The constant is uniform over those targets.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem (one-third Hölder stability of Brenier maps from a convex body) and sharpness of the exponent. Twelve definitions, including the Wasserstein distance and optimal maps, are Comparator holes filled from OpenAI's library.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization realizes finitely many positive diagonal affine maps of determinant one between rational solid boxes by a smooth compactly supported divergence-free flow. Source boxes are pairwise disjoint and target boxes are pairwise disjoint, while overlap between the two families is allowed. Each map holds on a neighborhood of the entire source box, and the velocity is supported in the middle half of the time interval.
rows.explanation: States the box-transport theorem of the current edition: finitely many diagonal affine maps of determinant one between rational boxes realised by one smooth compactly supported divergence-free flow.

rows.scope_quote: It also encodes every finite machine and input in a smooth, compactly supported incompressible Navier–Stokes flow on $\mathbb R^3$ starting from rest: the particle initially at $(4,0,0)$ enters the fixed open box $(-1,2)^3$ exactly when the machine halts. One velocity works for every viscosity $\nu>0$, with zero pressure and force $f_0+\nu f_1$. Velocity and force have bounded mixed derivatives and are one-periodic after time one; the repeated velocity depends only on the machine.
rows.explanation: States the balanced three-stack theorem: every machine and input is encoded in a smooth zero-data Navier–Stokes flow on R³ in which a fixed particle enters a fixed box exactly when the machine halts.

rows.scope_quote: It also encodes every finite machine and input in a smooth, compactly supported incompressible Navier–Stokes flow on $\mathbb R^3$ starting from rest: the particle initially at $(4,0,0)$ enters the fixed open box $(-1,2)^3$ exactly when the machine halts. One velocity works for every viscosity $\nu>0$, with zero pressure and force $f_0+\nu f_1$. Velocity and force have bounded mixed derivatives and are one-periodic after time one; the repeated velocity depends only on the machine.
rows.explanation: States the same balanced three-stack theorem as BalancedThreeStack: the two challenge files name the same theorem and library module and differ only in namespace layout and one instance declaration.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization proves that a fluid particle can detect arbitrary finite-machine halting using alternating-coordinate memory in smooth incompressible Navier–Stokes flows whose velocity and force decay faster than every inverse power of time, including every mixed derivative. For each fixed positive computable viscosity, the construction starts from rest and provides effective forces, unique material trajectories, and an exact equivalence between entering a fixed open detector and halting.
rows.explanation: States the rapid-decay paper's theorem on alternating memories: a fluid particle detects halting in Navier–Stokes flows whose velocity and force decay faster than every inverse power of time.

rows.scope_quote: The formalization constructs smooth forced three-dimensional Navier–Stokes flows from rest whose velocity fields detect whether a prescribed machine halts, at any positive computable viscosity. On the unit flat torus, halting is equivalent to the vertical velocity exceeding $1/2$ somewhere in a fixed observation strip. On $\mathbb R^2\times\mathbb T$, it is equivalent to the integral of the nonnegative vertical velocity over the observation half-plane times the circle exceeding $1/2$.
rows.explanation: States the main theorem of the velocity-detection paper: on the torus and on R² × T, halting is equivalent to a stated velocity threshold in a fixed observation region.

rows.scope_quote: This selected statement covers the sheet programs. The paper's fixed-particle halting detector and its reciprocal maps on solid boxes are outside its scope.
rows.explanation: States the paper's sheet theorem: finite families of positive diagonal maps on coding sheets realised by smooth incompressible flows on the three-torus. The paper's periodic-initialisation theorem with its fixed-particle halting detector is outside it.
